#### Timing

Movement starts after the first 100 ms tick. Releasing or cancelling before that
tick sends nothing. After a movement tick, cleanup sends its side-scoped STOP
with a fresh cancellation event. Explicit STOP remains available independently.
Presets, save buttons, massage taps and settings send once. Main writes are
serialized and spaced by at least 100 ms, avoiding the Android periodic-queue
race. Startup subscribes before Exit Limit, then schedules the nine product
queries at 50 ms producer intervals through that queue. Protocol version exactly
one schedules its seven additional information queries. No extra disconnect
packet is invented. USB switching retains its two-second throttle and delayed
second command; cancellation prevents a stale delayed write.

Blanket general temperature limits differ from its sleep-stage limits. Mite
removal changes local warm temperatures through the general clamp and sends
only the mite command. Sleep settings send before a changed main-mode frame.
The main delay keeps the app's raw multiply-by-sixty formula even though
its Android label says hours. Groove timers convert UI seconds to rounded
minutes before encoding; received timers retain the separate base-sixty decode
and subscriber multiplication. These values are not calibrated hardware units.

#### Notifications

The status sensor exposes capability pages, alarm records, direct-bed notification
fields, the local blanket model, saved choices and rejection details. Local
optimistic changes are not hardware acknowledgements. Alarm list replies append;
escalation replies replace the first record with the same number. General blanket
responses merge only the fields their subscribers consume. Unsupported RGB
colors retain palette index -1.

Common motor replies use `no`; extended replies use `position`. The latter stay
in diagnostics and do not silently overwrite the former. Malformed lengths,
truncated fields and stale notifications are rejected without reproducing Android
exceptions or nonprogressing loops. Unrelated desk/OTA payloads do not become bed
features. A product-menu reload can remove transient capability pages.

Sleep links use compact UTF-8 JSON over the shared sleep envelope. Sequence wraps
from 254 to 1; each write is split at the link's negotiated MTU minus three. MM
writes without response and HJ with response. Required and nullable response
fields remain distinct. Time replies update sleep type/version metadata. Report
metadata retains fsize-driven followups and polling cancellation; physiological
report interpretation is excluded. Local sleep cancellation clears the session,
without sending the main bed's movement STOP.
An active report keeps its BLE link through the metadata handshake and compressed
transfer, even when the link is released after each command or stays connected only briefly. Completion, cancellation,
disconnect, or a 60-second integration watchdog ends that hold. The watchdog is an
integration limit, not a protocol response interval.

#### Services

`adjustable_bed.richmat_app` exposes named configuration operations, validated
against the selected product and its current capabilities. Use normal device and
side targeting. The generated command reference and action form list operations;
no action accepts arbitrary packet bytes.

- Lighting: timer, palette/RGB and opacity, groove/color/breathe modes, power,
  therapy timer/color/sound and the local-music source.
- Alarms: single countdown, cancellation, explicit repeat slot, toggle, deletion
  and list refresh. Weekdays are Monday 0 through Sunday 6;
  7 means once. Full tables require an explicit slot and never emit Android's -1.
- Blanket: power, mode, selected-zone temperature, main delay, mite removal, all
  six settings flags and each zone's sleep schedule. Flags are child lock,
  protection, anti-freezing, tone, light and screen-off, in that order. A sleep
  schedule supplies its enabled flag, mode, start/end, repeat days, after-mode,
  delay and four stage temperatures. Schedule duration is validated together.
- Detection start/stop, anti-snore/off-bed settings, USB and cancellable automatic
  demos. Demo steps use known app enum names, sustain seconds and delay seconds.
- Separate sleep entry: time/part/realtime queries, polling,
  sensitivity query, automatic anti-snore query/setting, report session, init and
  local cancellation. `sleep_snore` uses value 0 for query and 1 for setting.
  There is no valid sensitivity setter in this app.
- Clock: the bed and the separate sleep entry set their clock with
  [Set bed clock](../SERVICES.md#sync_clock); the sleep entry also sets it on
  every connection.

#### Evidence

Richmat 4.2.0 provides every catalog, frame and lifecycle
value. `tests/test_richmat_app_vectors.py` preserves all 2,094 literal fixtures and
24 semantic cases. `tests/test_richmat_app.py` checks integration behavior.
Physical validation is for owners and is not implied here.

Every product offers head/foot movement, reset, two custom memories, TV,
zero gravity and anti-snore recall/programming; each preset's long press is its
**Save** button. Ultra adds combined head/foot, lumbar, pillow and massage. Elite
retains its direct bed-light button.
The normal light menu appears only after the connected bed reports it.

#### Timing

The generated table states the app intervals. Movement first refreshes after
one tick. Finite HA movement budgets start after that nominal startup tick,
with a fixed acceptance end anchored before waiting. New movement is accepted
strictly before that end, without queued catch-up or per-tick grace. Renewable
controls retain HA's absolute accepted hold lease. Cleanup begins at the finite
end (or earlier on STOP/cancellation), retains the source FIFO spacing and can
submit STOP after that end. The public action drains the submitted
write and its captured-link STOP even if the caller is cancelled. The app's
FIFO can leave older movement ahead of STOP; HA does not retain that backlog.
One-shot reset/massage/light actions have no additional release. Presets recall
once on a short press or save at the long-press threshold, suppressing recall.

#### Notifications

The status sensor exposes connection-scoped BED events, motor-index feedback,
massage, lighting, alarm records and lock state as attributes. Motor indices
and height-like values are retained without calibrated physical-axis claims.
Diagnostic and anti-snore configuration event payloads retain raw fields.
No setter is guessed from a receiver. Partial receive bytes expire and old
callbacks cannot publish into a replacement session. The app's exact snore
capability literal conflicts with its type-21 framing; no corrected frame is added.

#### Services

`adjustable_bed.bobpowerbase` exposes repeat alarm list/add/delete, light color,
light timeout and light off; [`sync_clock`](../SERVICES.md#sync_clock) sets the
local clock. Alarm actions are `anti_snore`,
`zero_gravity`, `tv`, `memory_1` and `memory_2`. Weekdays are Monday=0 through
Sunday=6; an empty list means once, and `enabled` occupies the low repeat bit.
New alarms use the first unused observed id from 1 through 7; this app allocation
range does not show the controller's capacity. An explicit `alarm_id` avoids
relying on an incomplete notification list. Light timeout accepts whole minutes
from 0 through 15, supplied as seconds, with zero selecting the always-on sentinel.
Color is two frames in one characteristic write. All requested targets and
operands are checked before control writes use the coordinator scheduler.

#### Analysis provenance

Based on Power Bob Base 1.0.9 (10900) (`com.richmat.bobpowerbase`).

### Majestic Home

**App:** [Majestic Home](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.majestichome) 1.0.4 (10400), `com.richmat.majestichome`

**Status:** Not yet tested

#### Setup

Choose **Majestic Home app · Richmat**, then the exact FARM, JLRM, JGRN or JHRN identifier
shown in the app. Change it later in Reconfigure. Each physical side of a
two-address pair keeps its own choice; separate a combined bed before changing
either side's product. Imports and restored entries use the same
profile id. The empty product sentinel has no controls and is not a setup choice.

The app scans without filters. A Bluetooth name or shared service cannot choose
its product. The six supported GATT definitions are listed in the codec transport
table. Service enumeration retains the first matching writable TX and the first
notify-capable characteristic; the declared RX UUID is metadata. The final matched
service selects raw versus framed commands even if earlier handles were retained.
Write-without-response is used only when that selected writable TX also advertises it.

The embedded manuals cover headboard installation, power storage, electric bed
controls and Hi-Lo Tilt. They inform labels only, not product-to-hardware
aliases, BLE pairing, side commands or packet values. The unused Factory Reset
title is not an action. Flat is the app's MotorReset control.

#### Controls

Native motor entities expose each product's held directions. Presets and their
separate save buttons, light toggle and every massage action are product-gated.
The massage timer keys are one **Massage timer** select (Off sends All Off), and
each zone's level keys are one head or foot massage number (0 sends that zone's
off key where the product has one).
Saving uses the source long operand with a single short action, not a timed long
press. There are no inferred brightness/RGB setters, calibration, position seeking,
extra memory slots, single-address split controls or factory reset.

Finite `timed_move` and `hold_control` actions require at least 200 ms. Their
elapsed budget includes the 100 ms delayed first tick and any radio pacing;
requests shorter than 200 ms are rejected. An implicit legacy one-pulse press
uses a 200 ms budget. Native cover presses keep their default duration. If radio
or scheduling delays consume the entire budget, HA reports failure without
sending expired movement. Renewable native holds keep their current absolute
lease expiry, with no startup allowance. STOP cleanup drains any submitted write
before releasing the same live physical link. These are HA safety bounds, not
new hardware timing guarantees or changes to the app's enqueue cadence.

#### Timing

The generated schedule gives first/refresh ticks and the clock-menu interval.
After notification registration, startup exits limit mode, sends the epoch/zone
and local calendar only for FARM/JLRM, then checks the clock menu. Alarm records
always put length before `20`, including over the raw Nordic route. Notifications
put length after `20`. All framed BED writes use additive sum8.
Epoch serialization takes the first eight padded hexadecimal digits; timezone
offsets truncate to whole hours and keep their low byte. The calendar uses the
local year minus 1970, month, day, hour, minute and second.

The app's sender is a periodic FIFO. Overlapping async callbacks can submit a
queued first item more than once, STOP does not flush it, and disconnect/dispose
does not explicitly STOP. HA serializes and drains the physical write before
movement cleanup, drops cancelled work and applies a strict elapsed hold ceiling.
It sends the actual STOP after a submitted held refresh, with cancellation unable
to suppress cleanup. A release before the first refresh sends nothing. Tap,
preset, save, light and massage actions send once without an extra STOP. These HA
ownership and cancellation guards are not a firmware watchdog.

#### Notifications

Common frames split at the next `6e` or consume the current buffer, without a
checksum gate or common-fragment assembly. The embedded-delimiter stop-music
literal cannot match through that stream. Extended BED frames accumulate their
declared length and validate sum8. No partial-record expiry is invented.
Malformed zero-length or truncated records are bounded instead of reproducing
the app's hang or indexing failure. Excluded OTA framing is consumed without an
updater. Desk, accessory and audio branches have no bed actions; shared BED
snore/out-of-bed and stop-music effects remain observations.

The diagnostic Model sensor (disabled by default) shows the product layout and
carries observed motor travel/angle, massage, white/RGB light, alarm, lock,
diagnostic and press/coupled/sync fields as attributes, without inferring physical
axes, units, firmware capabilities or setters. V1 checksum omission, ignored
extended motor index and raw diagnostic pass-through follow the source. All
observations and alarm fields are cleared on disconnect; old callbacks cannot
publish into a replacement physical session.

#### Actions

`adjustable_bed.majestichome` supports `list`, `new`, `set`, `toggle` and
`delete`; [`sync_clock`](../SERVICES.md#sync_clock) sets the clock. Alarm access requires the current connection's clock ACK.
FARM/JLRM supply the four preset choices. `set` creates or replaces an explicit
ID. `new` also requires an explicit ID from the app's range 1 through 7,
without claiming firmware capacity. A nonempty cache cannot show which slots
are free: the bed sends no list terminator or empty-list marker. Partial replies
and silence never authorize automatic allocation.

Weekday bits run Monday through Sunday from bit 7 to bit 1; bit 0 enables the
alarm. An empty weekday selection is once. New/edit forms use reserved zero.
Toggle preserves all received fields and changes only the enable bit, including
unknown preset and reserved values. Mutations mark cached fields stale until a
new notification arrives; ACKs do not invent the new tuple. Every target is
admitted before the first settings write, including native paired parent/child
device targets. A replaced session or changed alarm list invalidates the plan.
Sequential pairs preflight every physical target before any settings mutation.
An intentional switch retains only validated intent, never old packets or a
closed link. On the execution connection HA validates the owner/product and
inputs again, waits for the current clock ACK, and queries fresh target fields
for toggles. Changed toggle fields abort instead of reusing the previous tuple.
All topologies query a fresh requested-ID tuple before a toggle. Those reply
waits have a five-second HA bound; they do not confirm the list is complete.
An explicit list reads for five seconds from actual query submission, with slow
writes consuming that window. Its optional response contains copied alarm tuples
per physical address/side and `complete: false`, including for zero observations.
Sequential sides disconnect only after their observation window; the response
does not retain a live cache or confer mutation authority. Concurrent and
standalone plans retain their exact live-link guard.
Every target's actual entry route and physical ownership are checked again after
queued waits and at packet submission, before any settings mutation.

#### Evidence

Based on Majestic Home 1.0.4 (10400).


### L&P Adjustable Base

**App:** [L&P Adjustable Base](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.lp2) 2.3.25, `com.richmat.lp2`

**Status:** Not yet tested

#### Setup

Choose **L&P Adjustable Base app (newer version)**, then the layout printed on the
remote or
selected in the app. The `L&P-ADJBED` and `L&P ADJBED` names open a choice of
APRM or AQRM. A Bluetooth name or shared service offers an app hint, never a
physical left/right mapping. The special package service takes precedence
when both of its characteristics exist, then W1, W2, N1 and W4 are checked in
order. Third-service fallback requires the Advanced option.

#### Controls

Each selected layout supplies its own motion, presets, saves, massage, light
and extra controls. Saves use the card's save controls; long-press saves do not
become renewable holds. On/off pairs use switches. Fixed massage durations
use the **Massage timer** select. APRM has conflicting duration labels and retains
its individual timer controls. There are no app screen, arming or side pickers:
every command uses the first mode.

A bed takes either raw or framed commands, depending on its Bluetooth service.
A control whose command differs between the two is listed only for the bed's own
format, which is known from its first connection on and is remembered across
restarts. Before that, only the controls both formats share are listed.

#### Timing

Ordinary holds refresh at 150 ms, or 110 ms for TWRM/MLRM names. Raw 6BRM
refreshes at 170 ms. Held movement ends with STOP after 50 ms; one-shot and
short/long gestures release after 150 ms. Long thresholds come from the
selected layout. Cancellation abandons pending saves and keeps cleanup on
the admitted connection. Reconnect never receives an earlier command.

Framed initialization waits 300 ms after notification registration. Layouts
with alarm actions query the alarm capability, followed by light and aroma
queries, with 500 ms gaps. Alarm frames are 300 ms apart. Aroma settings
are 150 ms apart, and fan settings are 300 ms apart. RGB is one write
containing both color frames.

#### Notifications

The session parser accepts checksum-framed replies and discards callbacks
from previous connections. Alarm acknowledgements do not confirm a stored
schedule. Light and aroma settings need live capability replies. Table
height and range values stay in diagnostics; they are not bed motor angles.

#### Services

Use `set_alarm` for the selected layout's wake actions and supported preset/massage
combinations. The layout owns each selectable massage zone. Use `lp2` for color,
light duration (0–300 seconds), aromatherapy, fans and explicit control
gestures. The head fan sends duration then intensity.
The foot fan sends its intensity twice and does not transmit a duration.
Generic `richmat_classic` actions provide
layout-bound massage popups, timer controls and table operations.

#### Evidence

Based on L&P Adjustable Base 2.3.25 (`com.richmat.lp2`). Hardware is not yet
tested. Wi-Fi, accounts and mesh network administration are outside the
integration.


### Galaxy Bed Control

**App:** [Galaxy Bed Control](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=nl.starinternational.galaxy) 3.3.0 (330002), `nl.starinternational.galaxy`

**Status:** Not yet tested

#### Setup

Choose **Galaxy Bed Control app** and the exact product code. Setup suggests the
app's advertisement mapping, then requires the selected product's own remote
when it opens a remote picker. MHRN offers H158B's HNRN/HQRN and H109's
M7RN/MJRN outcomes. V9RM and RNRN keep separate base, standard and splitHead
configurations. A constructor, Bluetooth UUID or similar name never substitutes
one product for another. Unsupported codes and the two standalone desk products
are refused. Each physical side keeps its own product and remote settings.

Discovery follows Galaxy's case-sensitive substring scan, with the platform's
prefix matchers as discovery hints. Manual setup remains available when a name
occurs only inside the advertisement. Advertisement prefix extraction uppercases
four characters; the MPE branch uses nine. Its explicit mappings are suggestions,
not protocol aliases. The Russian OTRM mapping is O0RM. Short names and unknown
products do not select a fallback layout. No app-owned PIN or authentication
handshake is required. A usable write and notification channel is required before
any command is admitted. Framing stays bound to the selected write characteristic; a later accepted service cannot change that characteristic’s dialect.

#### Controls

Every bed-command button retains its selected descriptor's short operand, long
operand, Nordic override and gesture. Distinct codes and configurations remain
independent even when their commands happen to match. Action IDs below identify
both normal buttons and the exact alarm actions a product admits. The product
catalog determines which IDs are offered; getter-only lists do not add controls.

The side selector offers only that product's declared sides. Commands, explicit
service sides and single-address paired children all pass the same side check.
Home Assistant captures the side and BLE connection for an entire gesture, so a
side change cannot redirect its release. E3RM, GXRM, JDRM, JFRM and JGRM retain
the memory-save latch for the seven named memory/preset actions, with GXRM TV's
exception. APRM, BRRM, YFRM and YGRM start in release mode. BRRM/YFRM/YGRM's
flagged replacement sends the None operand rather than silently ignoring it.
Local visual flags do not grant or revoke BLE capabilities.

D1RM/D9RM expose Off, 10, 20 and 30 minute massage countdown choices. A committed
choice sends once without an added release. Other app-labelled bed effects,
including hardware fan, heating, aroma, lock, synchronization and music-related
bed commands, retain their own catalog bytes. Phone torch, speech and navigation
widgets are local app actions and do not create BLE buttons.

#### Timing

A sustained control first sends after 100 ms, then refreshes while held. Only
those controls advertise renewable holds; a local memory latch can change a
sustained action to one long operand. Short presses send on activation. Long and
short-and-long gestures use the app's 3-second threshold. Release after an active
short or sustained gesture sends the ordinary side-scoped STOP, using a fresh
cleanup path that cancellation cannot suppress. Short-and-long and long gestures
retain the app's absence of that automatic release. Explicit Stop always sends
STOP. A command in flight cannot be retracted.

Writes are serialized and paced at least 100 ms after completion. Home Assistant
invalidates pending movement on cancellation rather than replaying the Android
FIFO's stale movement. It checks the current connection again after pacing and
ignores notifications from replaced links. There is no app-level automatic write
retry, normal-message fragmentation or invented startup command. Notification
remainders expire after 500 ms; malformed packets are discarded without blocking
subsequent commands or publishing invented values.

<!-- generated:galaxy-startup -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_codec_docs.py from the codec and profile data. Edit those, not this block. -->

Subscribe before initialization. Queue the applicable local time and sleep-name
records, then check clock and light on the 300 ms menu schedule. Sync the two
local time records only for a product with an alarm list; query the sleep
advertisement name only for the nine BLE-enabled bed products. The catalog keeps
each copied configuration’s own gates.

| Step | Framed / Nordic |
|---|---|
| Check clock | `6E 08 01 01 78` / `01` |
| Check light | `6E 0A 00 01 79` / `01` |
<!-- /generated -->

#### Notifications

The disabled-by-default Galaxy **Status** sensor exposes decoded events as attributes, including
motor/angle records, massage, lights, lock, fan, heating, atomization, alarm
acknowledgements and records, diagnostics and bed sleep-advertisement metadata.
Raw values retain their reported numbering and units; they do not create assumed
percentage sliders. Atomization retains both timer bytes. Empty blanket models
remain empty rather than reporting computations the app never stored. Diagnostic
and audio-related replies remain observable without starting phone audio or
creating separate accessory integrations.

Clock replies enable the alarm menu only when the current product has an alarm
list; PNRN also has its initial menu exception. Light replies require the current
product's light flag. The first admitted ASCII sleep-name reply is cached until
the link is reset. Only the nine BLE-enabled bed products admit it; the six
HNRN/HQRN/HSRN/HURN/M7RN/MJRN products also admit the bed's anti-snore settings.
Parser press-mode events do not change the local release, hold or memory flags.

Separate sleep monitors, network setup, cloud accounts, firmware updates, desk
screens and standalone accessories are not part of this bed profile. Their
shared framing cannot stall the bed notification stream.

#### Services

`adjustable_bed.galaxy` provides product-gated alarm scheduling/cancellation,
repeat slots, RGB, light timeout/off, massage countdown and bed anti-snore
settings; [`sync_clock`](../SERVICES.md#sync_clock) sets the clock. Use `single`,
`cancel_single`, `repeat`, `delete`, `alarms`, `enable_alarm`, `light_color`, `light_duration`, `light_off`, `massage_timer`,
`snore_switch`, `snore_count`, `snore_time` or `snore_query`. Alarm writes take an
exact action ID from the selected product's alarm list. Repeat alarms use slots
1 through 7, Monday 0 through Sunday 6, and an explicit enable flag. `enable_alarm` changes an observed slot’s enabled bit while preserving all six received fields, including the reserved field and weekday mask. Query `alarms` first. Validating
all targets precedes execution; connection-time capability replies are checked
again before a feature write. A freshly connected bed must report the relevant
capability before that setting is used.

The advanced settings use the Galaxy length-before-domain record form, distinct
from the length-after-domain records other apps use. RGB remains two checksummed
subframes in one write. No raw-command or separate-sensor service is exposed.

#### Evidence

The 48,642 ordinary frames are in `tests/fixtures/galaxy` and encoded by
`codec/richmat.py`; focused tests also cover advanced builders, parsers,
countdown commits and runtime transitions. Not yet tested on hardware; owners
can help confirm firmware, physical sides and release behavior with timestamped
captures.

Based on Galaxy 3.3.0 (`nl.starinternational.galaxy`).

### Luuna Rise / Power Cool

**Status:** Not yet tested

#### Known Models

Select the app first, then its exact four-character layout. Luuna Rise has its
own 604-layout catalog and Power Cool its own 586-layout catalog. An app name,
shared Bluetooth service or matching opcode does not mean a product match.
Luuna's H-series layouts include HKRM with its own Left/Right selector. AHRM's
one-shot action differs between apps; Luuna also has an H9RM reset-labelled
action that is absent in Power Cool. That label does not prove a factory reset.

#### Features

Layout-bound movement, combined movement, recall/save, massage, USB, fan, lock
and light-labelled controls retain the selected app's gesture and visibility
gates. Lock and vibration targets remain unknown. No motor position, battery,
model identity or general command acknowledgment is reported by these apps.
Settings provide RGB, lamp timers and the D1RM/D9RM/Y6RM timer utilities.
`set_alarm` sets the alarm countdown: one of the layout's positions as
`wake_action` (the wake modes are `wake_mode_1` and `wake_mode_2`, flat sleep
`flat_sleep`), optional `massage` with a zone, or `none` with `massage` for
massage alone. A position and massage pair the app has no alarm code for is
refused. A lamp capability reply reveals a timer number
entity without a reload. Its value is a local requested setting, not readback.

#### Detection / Setup

Search for **Luuna Rise** or **Power Cool Sleep System** in the Richmat app
question. Choose the layout that matches your app, including manual selection
for QRRM / Cool Touch / 209A05 devices. Layout and fallback settings belong to
one physical address. Stored choices and local preferences do not identify the
firmware. A shared name or service never selects either app automatically.
The third-service fallback remains an explicit advanced opt-in, with runtime
characteristics rather than guessed UUIDs. Standalone desk layouts are omitted.

#### Protocol Details

Both profiles use the [Richmat transports](#transports), in W1, W2, Nordic UART,
W4 order. The first present service wins; incomplete roles do not fall through.
Raw Nordic/fallback controls send the selected resource bytes, and a button
whose legacy operand has another function is listed by it, as in the
[classic apps](#classic-richmat-apps). Wrapped controls
send `6E 01 mode command sum8`. A raw mode choice adds no side bytes. Direct
structured settings bypass that wrapper on either route. No PIN, authentication
handshake, MTU negotiation or firmware query is added.

Successful local subscription on a wrapped route precedes initialization by
300 ms. Notification failure suppresses initialization and capability proof,
while ordinary bed controls remain usable. Settings query alarm capability
only when the layout has alarm choices, then lamp capability, 500 ms apart.
Replies are checked on the current connection; cached Android flags and handles
cannot authorize a new session.

#### Commands

Status 1 refreshes while held, status 2 is a one-shot with 150 ms release,
and status 3 offers short recall or thresholded long action. E3RM's local MEM
selector overrides status 3: normal recall refreshes while held; armed save
sends on the next poll; both end with the 50 ms release. Hold/Release overlays
are limited to BRRM/YFRM/YGRM. GVRM's uninitialized old-long field emits no foot
command. U3RM's selected tag changes its additional actuator bytes.

The table preserves exact layout eligibility. Hidden controls remain hidden
unless an app overlay reveals them. Resource names are app labels, not a map of
the motors. Short music actions are unavailable while the long lock-labelled
gestures remain available.

#### Alarm actions

Set the alarm with [`set_alarm`](../SERVICES.md#set_alarm). A layout accepts
only the controls the app can wake you with; about 140 of each app's 600
layouts have any. TV, Lounge, Zero Gravity, Anti-snore and Flat sleep are the
`wake_action` values `tv`, `lounge`, `zero_g`, `anti_snore` and `flat_sleep`,
M1 to M3 are `memory_1` to `memory_3`, and the two wake modes are `wake_mode_1`
and `wake_mode_2`. Massage 1 and massage 2 intensity up are the `head` and
`feet` massage zones, and both together (or the massage-on control) `both`. Add
`massage: true` with a `massage_zone` to a position, or use `wake_action: none`
with `massage: true` for massage alone. On UFRM, for example, `wake_action:
zero_g` with `massage: true` and `massage_zone: head` wakes you with Zero
Gravity and massage 1.

These are the most common sets:

| Layouts | Alarm actions |
|---|---|
| UFRM, XJRM, XKRM, XZRM, Z5RM | TV, Lounge, Zero Gravity, M1, M2, massage 1 intensity up, massage 2 intensity up |
| O7RM, V4RM, XYRM, Z4RM, ZFRM | TV, Anti-snore, Zero Gravity, M1, M2, massage 1 intensity up, massage 2 intensity up |
| AFRM, AGRM, AMRM, ANRM, XFRM | Zero Gravity, Anti-snore, TV, massage 1 intensity up, massage 2 intensity up |
| A9RM, DARM, WURM, Z6RM | TV, Anti-snore, Zero Gravity, massage 1 intensity up, M1, massage 2 intensity up, M2 |
| FHRM, G9RM, HLRM and HRRM (Luuna Rise only) | TV, Lounge, Anti-snore, Zero Gravity, M1 |
| XGRM, Y1RM, Y7RM, YQRM | Zero Gravity, Anti-snore, M1 |

For another layout, download the bed's diagnostics: `alarm_actions` lists the
layout's alarm controls.

#### Position Feedback / Notifications

The source recognizer's checksum, prefix order and partial/coalesced-message
behavior are preserved. Malformed input reports a bounded diagnostic rejection.
Exact alarm-capability, lamp-capability and alarm set/cancel replies update
current-session state. An alarm confirmation preserves the local selection;
it is not a schedule readback or general movement acknowledgment. Desk telemetry
and accessory messages do not create bed position or accessory entities.

#### Command Timing

Ordinary refresh is 150 ms, or 110 ms for actual advertised TWRM/MLRM names.
Raw advertised 6BRM uses 170 ms. Manual layout selection does not change cadence.
Long thresholds are 3000 ms or the selected node's 5000 ms override, counted by
worker polls. Held release waits 50 ms. Alarm writes are 300 ms apart. RGB sends
one 10-byte write with a 150 ms busy interval. Lamp time is 0 to 300 seconds;
zero has distinct slider (`FFFF`) and Save (`0000`) encodings with unverified
physical meaning. Y6RM's app timer labels differ from its resource names, so
they are retained as app choices rather than asserted firmware durations.

Ordinary holds use renewable leases where the selected gesture actually
refreshes until release.

#### Notes

HA cancels pending saves and clears stale gesture latches instead of allowing
Android's in-bounds CANCEL/pause behavior to resume movement. Release targets
the mode admitted with the gesture, so changing a live selector cannot redirect
STOP. Cleanup uses a fresh cancellation event; raw long-only paths with no
defined release end their pending refresh without inventing a STOP.

Wi-Fi, mesh administration, cloud/accounts, OTA, standalone desks, phone/media
controls and separate aroma/audio accessories are outside this bed integration.
Luuna's manufacturing layouts remain excluded; Power Cool's separately accepted
direct bed diagnostics are available only through their explicit layouts.

#### Analysis provenance

Based on Luuna Rise 1.0.13 (`com.richmat.luunarise2`) and Power Cool Sleep System 1.0.8 (`com.richmat.powercool`).

### Lady Americana / ACAA / STA Homecare / Zero Gravity family

**Status:** Not yet tested

#### Setup

Choose the app's own row, **Lady Americana app · Richmat**, **ACAA app ·
Richmat**, **STA Homecare app · Richmat** or **Zero Gravity app · Richmat**,
then its four-character layout. All four are listed in setup and Reconfigure. A shared Bluetooth name or
service suggests the family, and does not choose an app or physical layout.
Each receiver in a two-address pair keeps its own app, layout and saved choices.
There is no single-address Left/Right selector for these apps.

The fixed route priority is W1, W2, Nordic UART, then W4. The first present
service wins even if its characteristics are incomplete. An explicit advanced
option enables the source's third-service property fallback. HA resolves both
characteristics from the current session and rejects an incomplete route.
Android leaves write type unchanged; HA uses the selected characteristic's
advertised write properties. There is no authentication or position feedback.

#### Controls

The generated tables below retain every layout's ordinary, raw legacy and
loaded long operands. Status 1 refreshes a held command. Status 2 sends once.
Status 3 distinguishes short recall from a long command. A numbered memory
resource is available only on layouts that actually bind it; controls retain
their source resource names where icons and resource numbering disagree. On a
Nordic UART bed, a button whose raw legacy operand has another function is
listed by it, as in the [classic apps](#classic-richmat-apps).

The GVRM Head/Foot choice is local: Head reads the legacy short getter on both
transports, while Foot has a null getter. It is not a bed-side address. U3RM's
local axis selection starts at third; tagged preset releases select third,
fourth or fifth for later adjustments. Legacy-long attributes ignored by the
Android constructor are not alternate commands.

The separate generic BED requests correspond to the app's recognized-command
callbacks. They remain usable through `richmat_resource_bed`, independently of XML buttons and alarm choices. A
`memory_three` request does not certify a third physical slot. Use the normal
Stop action for movement release. `voice_stop_request` sends the app's separate
request and then the protocol release; it is not an emergency stop.
Speech recognition and microphone machinery are not part of the integration.

#### Timing

The generated timing values are milliseconds. Only an actual raw-route
advertised name with trimmed prefix `6BRM` selects the longer refresh. Choosing
that layout manually does not change timing. The Android long counter uses
integer division of its threshold by the refresh, followed by its sending tick;
it is not an exact hardware wall-clock deadline.

HA serializes commands, bounds finite holds by elapsed time, settles in-flight
writes, and sends required release cleanup on cancellation. A late write cannot
cause a backlog of refreshes after the deadline. A sequential two-link pair
cannot sustain a Both hold; single-side actions remain available. No hardware
simultaneous fan-out or automatic stop on disconnect is claimed.

Startup is a direct framed write before notification registration, without an
ACK/authentication gate. Raw connections have no startup write. The query action
sends the optional alarm query only for nonempty layout metadata, then LED and
shared accessory queries in order. The latter retains shared-channel effects
without exposing accessory configuration. Direct settings, queries, RGB and
alarms bypass movement framing and do not append movement release packets.

#### Notifications

The Android five-byte validator checks the current fragment, with a signed sum
compared to an unsigned final byte. Rejected data remains buffered. Exactly ten
accumulated bytes dispatch unchecked. An oversized retained buffer is cleared
when a new fragment starts with the header. HA preserves those within-session
compatibility rules, with a bounded receive budget and callbacks tied to the
current controller/session. Android's retained cross-connection accumulator,
stale-global close and drop/resume worker behavior are not safe HA ownership
rules.

Alarm metadata, the received capability flag and direct alarm navigation are
separate gates. LED support requires an actual current-session reply; saved
menus and default RGB values are not device feedback. RGB is one
concatenated write. The phone wheel drops updates while its sender is busy;
HA serializes explicit action requests. Timeout retains the source's byte-pair
folding rather than silently substituting a conventional 16-bit value.

The phone's alarm set ACK reads CURRENT UI choices and the CURRENT global
address, merges tags without removing stale keys, and stores no scheduled time.
Hydration follows layout order with exclusive bed choices and independent
massage choices. Cancel click clears the entire phone preference file before
BLE; cancel ACK removes only the current address's ICON key. These phone-cache
behaviors are not observed hardware schedules. HA keeps request state per bed,
records received events without attributing them to a pending request, and
rejects stale-session effects. It reports no invented angle, battery, firmware
or alarm-time feedback.

#### Services

`adjustable_bed.richmat_resource_bed` exposes `query`, `rgb`, `lamp_timeout`,
`massage_timer` and `bed_command`. The action validates every target before
execution, and STOP fences later writes on every target even while another
target is awaiting BLE.

`set_alarm` sets and cancels the alarm: one of the layout's positions as
`wake_action`, optional `massage` with a zone (`both`, `head` or `feet`), or
`none` with `massage` for massage alone. The status entity lists the layout's
alarm actions. An alarm time selects its next local occurrence, with an equal
time meaning the next day. Only the layout-owned combinations are accepted. Light timeout
requests are 0–300 seconds, with zero labelled keep on. The D1RM massage slider
uses its actual 0–5 callback mapping. Requested values are labelled as requests,
not device readback. Other layout actions use their named buttons and the
standard `hold_control` action; held buttons publish current card metadata.

#### Evidence

All four apps share the binding
domain, both movement formats and direct settings builders. The Richmat codec
reproduces their test vectors; the controllers use each member's product scope
and keep its limits. Hardware
motion, physical axes, memory effects and optional features remain unverified.

### Okimiki

**App:** [Okimiki](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.okimiki)
1.0.1 (10101), `com.richmat.okimiki`

**Status:** Not yet tested

#### Setup

1. Choose **Okimiki app · Richmat**.
2. Choose the product code the app shows: HCRN, IPRM, IQRM or KWRN. The bed's
   name does not tell them apart.

The product decides the memory, preset and alarm controls. The light and alarm
controls appear once the bed has connected and reported them. Configure keeps
the product; on a bed with two receivers each side keeps its own.

Choose **Okimiki app · Richmat**, then the exact product code shown in the app. Configure,
import and restored entries retain that product independently for each bed.
Shared Bluetooth names/services do not select a product. Case-sensitive scan
keywords match anywhere in the name; manual setup also accepts these candidates.

<!-- generated:okimiki-products -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_codec_docs.py from the codec and profile data. Edit those, not this block. -->

| Product | Axes | Memory slots | Alarm | Light |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HCRN | head, foot | 2 | none | RGB/timer after capability reply |
| IPRM | head, foot | 0 | none | RGB/timer after capability reply |
| IQRM | head, foot | 2 | single | RGB/timer after capability reply |
| KWRN | head, foot | 2 | repeat | RGB/timer after capability reply |
<!-- /generated -->

The first eligible fixed-UUID write and first notify-capable characteristic are
selected across recognized services. The last matched service selects raw
Nordic versus framed basic commands. Dedicated light, clock and alarm records
remain full frames on every route. There is no PIN handshake or position read.
A physical address exposes side 0 only. Two separately configured beds can use
Home Assistant's native paired devices with independent settings and sessions.

#### Controls

All four products expose head/back, foot/legs, combined movement and flat. The
product table and command table describe their memory and preset controls.
Lighting appears only after the connected bed reports its light capability.
The native RGB light and duration number show requested values; they do not
claim confirmed light-state feedback. Zero duration means always on. On KWRN the
Alarms diagnostic sensor (disabled by default) counts the alarm records read
this session and lists each slot's time, wake action, weekdays and on/off as
attributes. Other decoded events stay in diagnostics.

After discovery, the light and duration entities keep their registry identities
and customizations through an idle disconnect. They remain unavailable until
that physical bed reports light support again. Changing the address or product
starts a separate discovery; remembered identities never authorize commands.

<!-- generated:okimiki-controls -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_codec_docs.py from the codec and profile data. Edit those, not this block. -->

| Control | Recall byte | Save byte | Gesture |
|---|---|---|---|
| head_up | `24` | none | 100 ms held refresh, then STOP |
| head_down | `25` | none | 100 ms held refresh, then STOP |
| foot_up | `26` | none | 100 ms held refresh, then STOP |
| foot_down | `27` | none | 100 ms held refresh, then STOP |
| head_foot_up | `29` | none | 100 ms held refresh, then STOP |
| head_foot_down | `2A` | none | 100 ms held refresh, then STOP |
| flat | `31` | none | flat on down, STOP on release |
| memory_1 | `2E` | `2B` | save at 3 s, recall on early release |
| memory_2 | `2F` | `2C` | save at 3 s, recall on early release |
| lounge | `59` | `65` | save at 3 s, recall on early release |
| zero_gravity | `45` | `66` | save at 3 s, recall on early release |
<!-- /generated -->

#### Timing

Held motors start after the first tick and release with STOP. Flat sends its
command on press and STOP on release. A preset released before the save
threshold recalls once. Save fires at the threshold with no later recall or
STOP. Explicit save buttons wait for that same threshold and can be cancelled.
Subscription precedes ExitLimit and, where offered, clock synchronization;
clock/light checks follow once each. The BED queue spaces submissions without
app-specific retries. Duration changes retain the slider-end delay.

<!-- generated:okimiki-timing -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_codec_docs.py from the codec and profile data. Edit those, not this block. -->

| Operation | Interval |
|---|---|
| Held refresh and FIFO | 100 ms |
| Save threshold | 3 s |
| Menu query spacing | 300 ms |
| Light duration delay | 200 ms |
<!-- /generated -->

#### Notifications

Common notifications consume the entire available buffer. Extended inbound
records use `6E 20 LENGTH`, distinct from outbound `6E LENGTH 20`. Add/cancel
replies are alarm acknowledgments, never music or confirmation of a particular
scheduled time. Recurring list items and updates retain all returned fields.
Capabilities and observed alarms are cleared when their session ends. Local
RGB/duration requests may restore, but are never replayed on reconnect.

#### Services

`adjustable_bed.okimiki` exposes bounded presses, explicit saves, lighting,
IQRM's one-shot lounge alarm and KWRN's recurring list, add/edit, enable and
delete operations. [`sync_clock`](../SERVICES.md#sync_clock) sets the clock of
products with an alarm. Alarm actions require the clock
capability reply. HCRN and IPRM have no alarm page. These alarms stay on this
action rather than the shared `set_alarm`: that action does not yet keep the
safeguards these record edits need across a paired hand-over, between check and
write, and when Stop interrupts the check.

Read KWRN's list before editing or deleting by ID; the Alarms sensor shows the
received slots. An edit retains the returned reserved byte; omitted fields retain
the received values. Weekdays are names, Monday to Sunday; an empty list means
once, and leaving the field out keeps an edited alarm's days. The four modes are lounge, zero gravity, memory 1 and memory 2. Choose an
explicit `alarm_id` from 1 through 7 when creating a recurring alarm. The list
has no completion marker, so Home Assistant does not infer a free slot from
missing or delayed replies. The app's exhausted allocator serializes FF; that
case is kept in codec tests, but Home Assistant requires an explicit
slot instead.

A one-shot alarm uses the selected local time and a minute countdown; a positive
subminute interval rolls to the next day. Clock sync sends epoch seconds with
a truncated whole-hour timezone, then a local calendar frame. Service requests
retain their physical owner through acceptance, validation, writes and cleanup.

#### Evidence

The app's original and continuation frames match the production Richmat codec
byte for byte; no existing profile's frames change. Hardware behavior, effective
STOP, RGB/timer and firmware alarm execution still need testing on real beds.
Shared passive bed effects add no controls and assume no single-address pairing.

Based on Okimiki 1.0.1 (`com.richmat.okimiki`).

### Nisco

**App:** Nisco 1.1.1 (code 3), `com.richmat.nisco`

**Status:** Not yet tested

#### Setup

Choose **Nisco app · Richmat** explicitly. Auto uses the first four Bluetooth
name characters, lowercased, as the surface identifier. A saved explicit model
wins over the name. QRRM asks for a real model. The six short identifiers
3i/4i/4it/5i/6i/7i are dormant in this app and are not offered. Shared UUIDs and
brand names do not select this app. Configure, import and restore retain the
app/model profile; a two-address pair retains each physical side's selection.

Choose **Separate HJ_Bed sleep and intervention receiver** for the separate
sensing module. That receiver has no motor controls. Two physical bed addresses
can use Home Assistant's parent/Left/Right pairing. Transmit modes 0, 1 and 2
remain app modes and do not create single-address native sides. They and the
app's motor group are not entities: set them with the `richmat_mh_control`
action's `app_mode`.

#### Controls

The selected model's own ordered functions, aliases and page maps determine
motors, presets, recall/program slots, massage, locks and other bed controls.
The generated tables below list each app separately. Nisco CFRM retains its
catalog LOCK entry. The transmit mode changes ordinary command and release
frames. Snore intervention samples the current mode at the final dispatch
boundary, including a mode changed while its write waited for the BLE lane.
The dedicated `13`-family setting is separate from normal anti-snore recall/save.

Buttons are named by their command, as in the
[Richmat MH apps](#richmat-mh-apps); the catalog labels stay as recorded. For
example `Massage Head Intensity Inc` is Massage: Head Up, `Zg2 Back`/`Zg2 Set`
are Zero gravity 2 and Save Zero gravity 2, and `Ubl Off` is Under-bed light
off. A model with more than
one of `Massage 10Min`, `Massage 20Min` and `Massage 30Min` shows them as the
**Massage timer** select (durations only); a model with one keeps its button.

Nisco's light timer preserves the high and low duration bytes. Normal and
waist mattress controls are dormant, even though startup probes and shared
checksum/parser effects exist. Parsed mattress frames remain controller state;
the sibling's detailed offsets and controls are not borrowed.

#### Timing

Ordinary KEEP uses the selected widget's interval. Fixed-layout remotes use
150 ms refresh; their long-save gesture waits three one-second ticks and sends
a checksummed save, followed by the 150 ms release sequence. The generic
LONG-worker's malformed checksum-zero example belongs to a distinct path,
not a reason to corrupt all saves or assume firmware tolerance.
HA does not expose that raw threshold path, which no current Nisco widget is
shown to use. Ordinary programming and the separately attached, checksummed
fixed-remote saves remain available.

`set_alarm` writes the ordinary alarm page's two-phase frames 300 ms apart.
The app's mode page sends the same frames 150 ms apart; Home Assistant uses the
alarm page's timing for both.

Startup subscribes, waits 300 ms, queries the version, waits 300 ms, then runs
the old or new ordered query schedule with 300 ms slots. Aroma and speech
infrastructure probes are excluded; their schedule slots remain. Queries target
one physical receiver. Group membership and physical recipients are independent
of transmit mode.

HA bounds light timers to 0..300 seconds, finite holds to elapsed time and
renewable holds to the scheduler's current deadline. These are HA choices, not
Android validation or a hardware watchdog guarantee. In-flight writes drain
before cancellation cleanup; source-defined releases use an independent cancel
event and cannot migrate into a replacement BLE session.

#### Notifications

The shared classifier retains exact version handling, INIT checksum/length
gates, mode, signed angle, massage, memory and alarm/snore state. The identical
massage/UBL-lock prefix remains shadowed; no missing lock decoder is added.
Nisco's waist combined forms are 14, 15 and 19 bytes, distinct from MLILY
Supreme's 14, 18 and 19. Nisco has no detailed diagnostic result consumer or
mattress cache offsets.

The sleep receiver retains local rates, occupancy, movement, user mode and
intervention settings. The raw `Std` value is the disabled-by-default
diagnostic Left/Right sleep receiver state sensor. Wi-Fi, network/mesh administration, cloud,
accounts, firmware administration, scoring, reports and phone/media features
are excluded. A BED effect remains included even when its caller
sits beside excluded infrastructure.

#### Services

`richmat_mh_control` runs a control on the selected model's app page, named in
`control` as its button or the app shows it (a motor adds its direction, such as
`Pillow up` or `Back down`), its attached fixed-remote long-save caller, or an
included query. A name the model's page does not have is rejected. Standard preset/memory actions,
`set_alarm` and `richmat_mh_light_color` use the same family runtime. Service
acceptance captures all physical targets and STOP epochs before lazy imports.

#### Evidence

Based on Nisco 1.1.1 (3).

### MLILY Supreme

**App:** MLILY Supreme 1.3.1 (code 5), `com.richmat.mlily_supreme`

**Status:** Not yet tested

#### Setup

Choose **MLILY Supreme app · Richmat** explicitly. This is a separate profile
from MLILY Control and other same-brand integrations. The name rule and GATT
priority match Nisco's common domains. Unlike Nisco, the six short
manual surface identifiers are selectable. Choose the explicit normal-mattress
variant only for that app-selected extra; a powered initialization must still
arrive. Waist powered initialization accepts its own area. Configure and paired
side storage retain these choices independently.

#### Controls

Use this app's own table. CFRM lacks Nisco's catalog LOCK entry. Its dedicated
smart-light-lock caller is independently available on the accepted CFRM light
page, preserves fixed mode 00 and sends once without motor release.

The light timer's final high byte is the current transmit mode, including its
zero-duration form; it is not Nisco's duration-high-byte behavior. Motor target
and massage builders preserve their own masks and packed fields. Normal
mattress pressure, warmth, zone, duration, mode, leg/pillow movement and alarm
controls require the normal-mattress selection and initialization. Waist mode,
warmth, pressure, duration and alarms retain their separate left/right/both
setting domains. Pad selectors do not create another BLE recipient.

The pressure and duration selects (mattress pressure, heat duration, pillow
duration, waist pressure and waist duration) offer only what the app's dialogs
send, so they have no Off: a reported zero shows as unknown. Heat is turned off
with the heat level, and the pillow is lowered with its own control.

#### Timing

The shared query schedule and ordinary/fixed-remote caller timings apply only
where the app uses them. Two-phase alarms use 300 ms. Mattress initialization
consumers run 300 ms after their accepted frames. Mattress commands are one-shot;
mode zero and leg/pillow zero are explicit stop values.

#### Notifications

The diagnostic INIT decoder checks exact capability, start and stop replies
before result-prefix decoding. Results use the low nibble of byte 2, high
nibble of byte 3 and low nibble of byte 3. The guarded consumer appends recognized
motor1..5, massager1..2, UBL and controller USB results. Repeated components
remain repeated rows; unknown type/number pairs append nothing. Unknown result
nibbles remain raw. Only result 1 is a pass. Start clears rows and resets progress;
stop resets progress and retains rows. Other valid INIT frames keep their generic
fallback. The source length/checksum gate covers the whole accumulated buffer.

Normal/waist cache keys, alarm tails and the source's fixed-end-index resync
quirk remain distinct from Nisco's. Coalesced waist lengths are
14, 18 and 19 bytes. The separate sleep receiver's live consumer requires a
saved physical receiver; `Std` defaults to 1. HA rejects signed-length overflow
headers and bounds malformed buffering rather than claiming Android recovered
those inputs. Bleak owns subscription descriptors; HA does not write arbitrary
non-CCCD descriptors. Missing preferred characteristics fail safely, without a
guaranteed Android fallback-recovery claim.

#### Services

The family control and light-color actions and `set_alarm` target the
selected physical bed or paired child. Every target is validated before the
first control frame, and stale ownership or a later STOP invalidates acceptance.
No Wi-Fi, SSID, mesh, cloud, account, OTA, audio or accessory administration
service is provided.

#### Evidence

Based on MLILY Supreme 1.3.1 (5).

### SleepEvolution / W.Silver Products 3.x

**Status:** Not yet tested

| App | Version (code) | Package ID |
|---|---|---|
| [SleepEvolution](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.nu503) | 3.5.5 (13) | `com.richmat.nu503` |
| [W.Silver Products](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.silver) | 3.3.7 (9) | `com.richmat.silver` |

Physical directions, preset, massage, light and reset effects, radio delivery
and STOP response are not yet verified on hardware.

#### Setup

1. Choose **SleepEvolution app · Richmat** or **W.Silver Products app (older
   version) · Richmat** (W.Silver Products 3.x).
   The newer W.Silver Products app is a separate choice.
2. Choose the start of the bed's Bluetooth name (**Bed model or remote**). It is
   case-sensitive. A6, U3, U5 and X1 are offered only for SleepEvolution.

**Reconfigure** asks the same two questions. On a bed with two receivers, add
each one and combine them; each keeps its own app and name. Left and Right
controls on one receiver are not supported. **Read bed position** is off.

Search for **SleepEvolution app · Richmat** or **W.Silver Products app (older
version) · Richmat** in setup or **Reconfigure**, then select the exact case-sensitive two-character name
prefix. A matching name can suggest a prefix only after app selection. Shared
prefixes and Nordic UART services cannot choose between the apps. The newer
W.Silver MH app remains a separate choice. `Ml`, `Mr` and `Ms` are case
sensitive; `0B` is an alias for M4. A6, U3, U5 and X1 belong only to
SleepEvolution. BE includes its separate massage screen.

Each receiver in a two-address pair keeps its own app and prefix. The apps have
no bed-side field, so single-address paired addressing is unsupported. A
sequential connection cannot run a held batch on both sides. HA owns Bluetooth
adapter/proxy discovery, connection acceptance and handoff.

#### Controls

| Feature | Availability |
|---|---|
| Movement | Paired head/foot direction graphics are covers. Other direction graphics are held buttons named for what they show (Head and foot up, Upper Section Up, ...), without guessing the physical motor count. |
| Presets and memory | Exact named actions in the selected profile, including separate Save buttons where the app can save. No universal slot count or numeric memory namespace. |
| Massage and bed light | Profile-specific request buttons; local icon/flag changes do not confirm remote state. Where a remote has more than one fixed massage timer key (10MIN, 20MIN, 30MIN), they are the **Massage timer** select, with durations only; **Massage timer / off** stays a button. |
| Factory Reset | Only where listed; requires confirmation in the native card, as do Save buttons. |
| Position and device state feedback | None. |
| Renewable holds | Motion controls only. Countdown, massage, programming and local selectors remain finite. |

The command tables below describe raw single-character ASCII String bytes over
Nordic UART. There is no packet envelope, terminator, checksum, sequence, side
field or authentication exchange. Each listed byte is a separate write,
including adjacent triplicate recalls, with no added interwrite delay. `$` is
byte `24` and character `1` is byte `31`; uppercase and lowercase commands
remain distinct. The live characteristic's properties select ATT write mode;
radio delivery remains still needs testing on hardware.

Control keys identify the selected profile's app labels/artwork, rather than a
universal command map. For example, A1 and A2 recall the same displayed slots
but have different M2/M3 save associations. BZ's displayed M2/M3 associations
also remain exactly as listed. The source field name alone does not identify a
control: M5's `h26_flat` is bed-light artwork.

GV's head/foot flag selects an axis, never a bed side. SleepEvolution defaults
to foot (flag 1); W.Silver defaults to head (flag 0). Home Assistant has no axis
picker: GV's position, massage power and +/− controls are separate Head and
Foot buttons that choose the axis, then press. Likewise U3's selected-axis
arrows are Lumbar, Tilt and Lounge Up/Down buttons for modes 1, 2 and 3. Their GV periodic maps and
schedules differ, including W.Silver's off pictogram with no periodic write.
Use only the chosen app's table. U3 starts in mode 0; its local lumbar selector
selects mode 1, while mode 2/3 selectors also perform the listed bed writes.
U5's LED request flag alternates locally. These choices reset with the physical
session and are not confirmed device state.

States without a listed timer arm have no periodic write. **Bed release
gesture** retains the direct bed effects of phone-torch handlers: `m`/`n`,
release only, or cancellation only as listed. Phone torch is excluded and is
never exposed as a bed light or phone control. Local-only selectors and
cancellation-only actions send no wire packet of their own. These, controls
that send only the `m`/`n` wake and release (such as the release gesture) and
U3's tilt selector (the Lounge recall without its release) remain
`richmat_legacy` action controls but are not buttons. Network, SSID,
password, cloud, account, OTA and unrelated phone, audio, accessory and seating
functions are excluded from these direct BLE bed profiles.

#### Timing

The generated catalog lists each screen's initialization delay and period.
Timers start from screen initialization, not universally from DOWN. HA creates
separate per-screen epochs and local flags for each physical session, including
BE's motor and massage screens, and activates a control only while a serialized
operation owns it. The next eligible event can occur almost immediately.

Motion with only `m` on DOWN waits for its first actual movement refresh before
its requested active elapsed window starts. Slow writes consume that window;
missed refresh intervals are skipped rather than backfilled. Other finite wire
gestures retain their requested DOWN-to-release separation. A missing timer arm
does not acquire a repeated command.

Short recall and long save use independent event-count guards, not one common
wall-clock duration:

- Threshold 20 first sends save on event 21. A short guard `<15` permits recall
  at counts 0–14, leaving events 15–20 with neither recall nor save.
- Threshold 15 first sends save on event 16. With the same short guard, event 15
  has neither recall nor save.
- Further eligible events repeat save during a deliberate long gesture. The
  dedicated **Save** action instead stops after the first completed save write,
  within a bounded budget of `(threshold + 2)` periods plus five seconds,
  measured from the next eligible timer event.
- Counter reset is per control, as shown in the local-effects column. There is
  no universal counter reset on DOWN or shared counter between receivers.

Release remains control-specific, including the count gaps. M4 lounge, M9 ZG
and Touch3 (T3) lounge retain unconditional `n` (`6E`) after long holds. A6 ZG
retains its extra short `n`; U3's mode-2 selector retains no release. LP's
explicit STOP request remains distinct from ordinary release. No global
command deduplication changes these events.

Cleanup uses the captured physical connection and a fresh cancellation event.
Already-submitted GATT work and the complete release batch drain independently
of cancellation; unconditional cleanup is attempted even if a short-recall
write fails. A stale callback cannot write to a replacement bed. These rules
do not guarantee a mechanical stop.

#### Notifications

The apps declare a local notify target but no application subscription
handshake, ACK parser, position schema or device-state feedback. HA does not
enable a peripheral subscription merely because Android locally enabled
notifications after writes. There are no startup, read, authentication or
position-query packets.

#### Services

`adjustable_bed.richmat_legacy` runs a listed `control` with a finite
`operation: gesture`, or `operation: program` for a save. Gesture
`duration_ms` is 1–60000, default 1000; program uses its event budget instead.
Programming cancellation suppresses short recall. Finite `hold_control`
gestures retain their original recall/save boundary; renewable holds accept
motion only. All batch targets pass acceptance before writes.

Use named catalog actions for the displayed memory slots, rather than generic
numeric memory services. See [Actions and Automations](../SERVICES.md#richmat_legacy)
for fields and an A1 recall/save example. There is no arbitrary-command interface.

#### Evidence

Based on SleepEvolution 3.5.5 (13) and W.Silver Products 3.3.7 (9).


### SleepFunction Bed Control

**App:** [SleepFunction Bed Control](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.sleepfunction) 1.3.0, `com.richmat.sleepfunction`

**Status:** Not yet tested on hardware.

#### Setup

Choose **SleepFunction Bed Control app** in the Richmat app picker and search for
its four-character layout. Choose the child layout directly for the ZRS0–ZRS3
picker screens. Reconfigure uses the same choices. The actual GATT
table selects FEE9/FB, FEE9/BB, Nordic UART, then FFF0 in that order. A missing
characteristic on the first matching service fails setup. The third-service
property fallback requires the explicit Advanced option. No PIN or clock
synchronization is used. A shared service or name never identifies this app.

#### Controls

Movement, presets, memory saves, massage, lock and synchronization follow the
selected layout's own resources. Preset saves ask for confirmation; memory saves
use the card's Set mode. Controls
hidden by the layout stay hidden; the separate save buttons on YFRM, YGRM and
BRRM appear in continuous mode. **Continuous movement** sends the app's Hold or
Release command and changes the effective preset gestures. Native buttons carry
their own mode or side. Scoped movement actions keep their full names in
Utility, and scoped memory actions are separate presets with confirmed saves.
Raw Nordic writes ignore the mode, as in the app.

RGB lighting and its 0–300 second timeout appear after a valid LED reply.
The **Massage timer** select offers the slider's four stops on D1RM and D9RM (off, 10, 20 and 30 minutes: the same three commands the popup shows as 10, 20 and 30 minutes, although the slider's own stop labels read 0, 2H, 3H and 5H; the real duration is not verified on a bed),
and 10, 20 or 30 minutes on layouts with the timer popup, which has no
idempotent off. There is no measured bed position feedback.

#### Timing

The actual Bluetooth name selects 170 ms for raw 6BRM, 110 ms for TWRM or MLRM,
and 150 ms otherwise. Selecting a layout does not change that interval.
Framed startup follows notification registration by 300 ms. Optional settings
queries are spaced 500 ms apart. A held control releases after a 50 ms delay;
a once or short press releases after 150 ms. Long actions retain their own
3,000 or 5,000 ms threshold. On framed links, releasing a long-only control
also schedules END after 50 ms; raw long-only release adds no frame.

Home Assistant cancels refreshes and finishes release cleanup on cancellation.
Cleanup belongs to the original native controller and BLE session. A reconnect
or layout change cannot receive an older action or its release.

#### Notifications

The checksum-checked, ordered-prefix parser consumes fragmented five-, seven-
and sixteen-byte replies. Alarm, LED and aroma capability replies are scoped
to the current session. Malformed input is bounded and discarded. Desk replies
never become bed position sensors. Alarm acknowledgements do not prove a saved
schedule or its target time.

#### Services

Use **Set alarm** for the selected layout's presets and supported massage
combinations. The bed receives relative minutes in two frames 300 ms apart.
**Set SleepFunction bed settings** sends head/foot fan or aroma settings.
Aroma durations are 1–60 minutes and its pause is 1–12 hours. Fan duration is
0–6 hours and speed is 0–100 percent in steps of 20. The foot fan path sends its
speed twice and does not transmit the selected time. Aroma writes are 150 ms
apart and fan writes are 300 ms apart.

#### Evidence

Based on SleepFunction Bed Control 1.3.0. The raw, framed, RGB, alarm, aroma and
fan builders reproduce the app's literal frames. Physical actuator wiring,
END's stopping effect and optional features still need user hardware captures.

### BedSmart / X-Series

**App:** [X-Series](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.bedsmart) 1.0.7 (8), `com.richmat.bedsmart`

**Status:** Not yet tested

#### Setup

Choose **BedSmart / X-Series app** in the Richmat app question, then choose the
four-character layout matching the app. **Reconfigure** changes the app or
layout later. Each physical bed in a combined pair keeps its own choices.
Name matches offer the app as a choice; they do not identify a physical model.
The manual aliases B6RU and ZR90 work without being automatic scan prefixes.
ZRS0, ZRS1, ZRS2 and ZRS3 are menus: choose the matching destination layout
during setup. If a layout correction cannot use a saved selection, that
selection returns to the layout's defaults.
Use the advanced third-service fallback only for a receiver whose GATT table
requires it. The first existing fixed service owns both characteristics.

| Field | Choices | Purpose |
|-------|---------|---------|
| Bed layout | Shipped four-character layouts | Select the app's controls |
| Third-service fallback | Off / On | Explicit property-based raw transport |

Nine layouts have an app selector labelled Left and Right; six label it Mode 1,
Mode 2 and Mode 3. On a bed that takes framed commands it is a select:
**Controlled side** (Left / Right) or **Bed mode** (Mode 1 / Mode 2 / Mode 3).
Choosing sends nothing; every later command carries the choice as 0, 1 or 2,
and it is remembered across restarts. Raw commands carry no mode, so a raw bed,
or one not yet connected, has no select. There is no Both selector or
single-address pair capability. Physical side behavior has not been tested.

#### Controls

The layout owns its motor, preset, recall, save, massage, light, sync and lock
controls. Preset saves ask for confirmation; memory saves use the card's Set
mode. Saves do not accept a renewable hold. Extras
start disabled. A toggle-only light offers an optional estimated on/off light.
Massage durations use the **Massage timer** select. D1RM and D9RM offer
the slider's four stops on D1RM and D9RM (off, 10, 20 and 30 minutes: the same three commands the popup shows as 10, 20 and 30 minutes, although the slider's own stop labels read 0, 2H, 3H and 5H; the real duration is not verified on a bed).
Y6RM offers the popup's 10, 20 and 30 minutes, with a **Toggle massage timer**
button for the popup's timer on/off button.
E3RM separates sustained recall from immediate saving. YFRM, YGRM and BRRM
offer separate tap and held recall, with explicit save buttons.
U3RM's two selected-motor buttons appear once per motor, as Motor 3, Motor 4
and Motor 5 up and down, instead of the app's motor selector. GVRM's head or
foot buttons always send their head command: the app has no foot command for
them. GVRM's Set key is **Program**: it arms programming and saves nothing by
itself, so it starts disabled and still asks first. As with L&P, a control whose command differs between raw and framed beds
is listed only for the bed's own format, once that is known.

#### Timing

The generated tables show the advertised-name refresh and per-control long
thresholds. Held controls stop after a finite duration or the active hold lease.
Release waits 50 ms after continuous movement, or 150 ms after a tap. The
original session and mode own cleanup, including cancellation. Catalog, address
or transport changes cannot inherit an old release. Timing and idle changes
still permit STOP on the same retained physical session.

#### Notifications

The parser checks each reply's checksum and recognizes alarm, light and aroma
replies. It clears and trims its buffer the way the app does.
Discovered lighting and aroma controls remain available across reconnects. Each
new connection must report support before a settings write; a remembered control
is not permission to write without that reply.
Replies may enable optional controls, but alarm acknowledgements do not prove
a stored schedule. Invalid notifications are contained and the receive buffer
is bounded. Lift-only responses do not become bed position feedback.

#### Services

Use `adjustable_bed.set_alarm` for layout-owned wake actions and massage
combinations. It sends a relative-minute alarm in two writes, 300 ms apart.
Use **Refresh bed features** to issue settings queries. The
[`adjustable_bed.bedsmart`](../SERVICES.md#bedsmart) action offers RGB color, light timeout, aroma times,
and the app's named BED commands. It
preflights all selected beds before writing. Alarm and feature controls never
expand a layout from a shared UUID. There is no clock synchronization command.

#### Evidence

Based on BedSmart / X-Series 1.0.7 (`com.richmat.bedsmart`): the layout
operands, raw old-short overrides, framed controls, direct auxiliary frames,
parser and event timing. Hardware is not yet tested.


### Bed Tech

**App:** Bed Tech 2.8.3, `com.richmat.bed_tech`

**Status:** Not yet tested

#### Setup

Choose **Bed Tech app (older app) · Richmat**, then your model. This is separate from the modern
**BedTech app (newer app)** and its legacy controls. Automatic uses the first four Bluetooth
name characters. **Cool Touch** and **QRRM** ask for a model. Short model names
such as **5I** require an explicit selection. BT3000 and BT3000FH select the same
controls. Combine two Bluetooth devices to control separate physical sides.

The model survives Configure, Reconfigure, import and restore. Two physical
addresses can be paired with Home Assistant's parent and Left/Right devices;
each side retains its own app and model. App transmit modes 0, 1 and 2 are
separate from physical bed sides. Set them and the declared motor group with
`richmat_mh_control`, using `action: app_mode`.

Choose **Separate sleep and intervention receiver** for the auxiliary
receiver. It exposes local single/double user mode and left/right intervention
switches, with its own BLE session and clock. It has no motor controls or
physiological report entities. Its intervention settings are not known to move
the bed. Normal mattress controls require the explicit
normal-mattress option and powered initialization; waist controls require the
receiver's waist initialization.

#### Controls

The selected surface determines motor directions, presets, memory recall and
save, massage, lighting, aroma and alarm options. Version 1 entity pages use
only their own typed controls. Generic 5I includes combined down; GRRM and BPRN
keep their selected-tab up-only behavior. In the 3I entity page, saving M3 sends
the app's M4-save code. Pillow and lumbar names follow the app's typed mapping.

On CFRM, the light lock state the bed reports is a sensor, disabled by
default; the light lock has no toggle command, because the app's button for it
sends nothing. The motor-page lock command is separate. Snore acknowledgements
and the selected intervention are separate states: the bed reports its snore
mode in its normal reply, and a successful write shows the commanded mode; the
initialization reply does neither.

Use the shared **Set alarm** and **Set bed clock** actions. Supported surfaces
choose countdown, three-slot or calendar alarms; mattress alarms remain
separate. Calendar saves and disables read slots from the bed and preserve the
reported bed identifier. A native request needs one unambiguous slot; no fixed
capacity is assumed. Disabling preserves the latest time, days and wake mode.
Disabled-by-default **Refresh alarms** and confirmed **Delete alarm** buttons
manage the reported records. Deleting withdraws that slot until bed readback.
Known delete buttons keep their identities across reconnects and wait for
current-session readback to become available.
No app-clock buttons or raw packet controls are exposed.

#### Timing

Held controls refresh at their declared interval, normally 100 ms. Release and
ordinary one-shot completion send the app's END frame after 120 ms.
Home Assistant bounds held movement and drains release before allowing the next
command. It captures the physical connection and transmit mode before waiting
and rejects stale commands and callbacks. END's physical effect is unverified.

Notifications start before the 300 ms version probe; initialization starts
300 ms later, with 300 ms task spacing for the generic route and 400 ms for
version 1. Primary writes use the selected
characteristic's supported write mode. The auxiliary receiver paces writes
300 ms apart, retries notification setup up to three times and uses a five-second
heartbeat. These are the app's intervals, not timings measured on a bed.

#### Notifications

Motor angles preserve signed-byte interpretation and declared display offsets;
malformed double-negative values are ignored. Capabilities on entity pages
reset on each initialization reply rather than accumulating. Calendar records
preserve decimal slot/bed parsing and signed times; repeated records are retained
as observations while the latest record supplies each actionable slot.
Calendar records that are too short are dropped; whether another incomplete
reply is held until it is complete depends on the reply type. Connection state is cleared
when a link is reused.

Wi-Fi, network administration, cloud accounts, group administration, firmware
updates, audio, phone recognition infrastructure, manufacturing/test paths,
desks and unrelated physiological reports are outside this integration. A
bed action the app's voice control sends is available where the selected model
also has it as an ordinary control.

### Jerome's Adjustable Base

**App:** Jerome's Adjustable Base 1.0.3, `com.richmat.jeromesadjustablebase`

**Status:** Not yet tested on hardware

#### Setup

Choose **Jerome's Adjustable Base app** and select the model printed on the bed.
The app searches Bluetooth names containing `QRRM`, `COOL`, `MPE_`, `209A`
or `BED-`. These names are shared with other Richmat apps, so the model is an
explicit choice. Reconfigure to change it.

The integration uses the single matching service from [Transports](#transports)
and the first characteristic that advertises notifications on that service.
A connection with several matching services requires a GATT trace to determine
its encoding. SH models have a **Controlled side** selector on the framed
connection. The selector uses the same Bluetooth address and service for both
sides. Nordic UART control has a single destination. Changing the selector
affects commands admitted after the change.

| ELEVATE 2.0 SH | `HERN` | 1 | No | Repeat |
| WAVE | `HDRN` | 2 | Yes | Countdown |
| WAVE SH | `JERN` | 2 | Yes | Repeat |
<!-- /generated -->

#### Controls

Head, foot and combined movement have renewable holds. Releasing a hold sends
STOP on the same selected side, even when release comes before the first
movement. Flat and preset recall each send one command. The save buttons and
memory programming wait for the app's save threshold before writing.

Wave models add massage intensity steps for the head and foot, pattern cycling,
off and a timer. A Wave bed that answers the light probe also offers toggle,
white selection and an auto-off timer. The light's colour and timer settings
apply to the receiver.
