#### Notifications

The clock reply opens alarm controls. On the countdown models the bed's
save and cancel acknowledgements update **Bed alarm status**. On SH models,
the sensor lists records the connected bed reports. Exact duplicates in a
list are ignored. An update replaces the first record with the same slot.
A partial notification expires when another fragment fails to arrive within
the receive window in the timing table.

#### Services

Use [`sync_clock`](../SERVICES.md#sync_clock) to send local calendar time and
[`set_alarm`](../SERVICES.md#set_alarm) to set an alarm. The non-SH models
count down to the next occurrence. On SH models, choose the slot and weekdays
to add or replace an alarm. Empty weekdays schedule it once. For SH alarms,
setting `enabled: false` changes the enabled bit of the alarm the bed reports
for that slot. Saving an edit refreshes the list, so a subsequent disable uses
the newly reported record.

Use [`jerome_repeat_alarm`](../SERVICES.md#jerome_repeat_alarm) on an SH model
to list, enable or delete stored alarms. Enabling preserves the other values
reported by the bed. Run `list` to pick up schedules changed outside Home
Assistant. After a local edit or deletion, the refresh may reconnect first
to ensure that old replies cannot be used for the next change.

### Jerome's power base

**App:** Jerome's power base 1.0.9, `com.richmat.jerome2`

**Status:** Not yet tested

Jerome's power base uses a separate layout catalog from the other Richmat apps.
Shared Bluetooth services do not identify the layout. Movement, presets, saved
positions, massage, light and aroma controls follow the selected layout. Optional light and aroma settings appear after discovery and
remain configured while idle. Writes require a reply on the current connection.
There is no motor-position feedback, inferred physical
mapping for additional motors, or inferred preset capacity.

#### Setup

Choose **Jerome's power base app** in the Richmat app picker, then search the
layout list. Use **Reconfigure** to change the app or layout. If the Russian app displays
`OTRM`, choose `O0RM`, the layout that language route opens. The advanced
third-service option permits the app's property-based fallback when the four
fixed routes are absent. The selected characteristic must be writable. The original Bluetooth name
is required to select the app’s refresh interval; the chosen layout does not
substitute for that name.

Use native combined-bed Left and Right targets for the seven layouts that
label those sides, on a framed connection. The parent’s Both target sends each
side’s command in turn. Other layouts with three modes
accept `mode: 0`, `1` or `2` on the `jerome_bed` action. The raw connection does
not encode a side or a nonzero mode. Direct alarm, RGB, aroma and duration
frames have no side field, so whole-bed settings require a standalone physical
bed entry. They are not offered on one-address combined-bed children. Two-address
combined beds retain each physical bed’s settings.

#### Controls

The entities expose named actions, inverse on/off pairs as switches, known
light state through the light platform, the **Massage timer** select (the
slider's four stops on D1RM and D9RM: off, 10, 20 and 30 minutes, the same
three commands the popup shows as 10, 20 and 30 minutes although the slider's
own stop labels read 0, 2H, 3H and 5H,
so the real duration is not verified on a bed; 10, 20 or 30 minutes on Y6RM,
whose popup has no idempotent off), and the layout's real intensity range where
present. Aroma
times are configuration entities, disabled by default. Save controls use the card’s guarded Set mode or an explicit confirmation,
and never support renewable holds. The `jerome_bed` action can request a layout
action, a supported continuous gesture, or its explicit long-press variant.

On a Nordic UART bed, a control whose legacy operand has another function is
named by it, as in the [classic apps](#classic-richmat-apps). The light key of
A3RM, BERM, MMRM and R2RM sends a movement or massage operand there, so those
beds get no under-bed light.

For `U3RM`, named position-adjustment controls capture the corresponding
selection for that action. Selecting a position never changes the meaning of a
later, unrelated movement command. Layout-navigation screens are represented
by explicit layout selection, rather than dashboard page-state entities.

Use `set_alarm` for a selected-layout wake position, optional massage or the
layout’s wake mode when offered. An equal target minute means the next day. The alarm is a
one-shot countdown, not a clock-synchronized weekly schedule. Acknowledgments
are diagnostic events and do not prove a stored alarm time or selected action.

#### Notifications

The streaming parser recognizes alarm set/cancel acknowledgments and alarm,
light and aroma capability replies. Light replies distinguish on and off.
The app does not read aroma settings back correctly, so Home Assistant shows no
aroma readback. No normal-bed position or massage
state decoder is defined. Malformed packets are recorded diagnostically.

#### Cleanup

Home Assistant keeps each command on the connection and target it started on,
sends one write at a time, finishes a write in flight before cleanup, and drops
a pending long press between actions. A gesture never carries over to a new
connection.

The raw lock controls on `AORM` and `E9RM`, and the synchronization controls on
`DXRM`, have no short operand or release frame; their framed counterparts use
the held-release delay. On the raw path, cleanup ends the pending writes
without a release frame, as the app does. An explicit Stop still sends the
normal release.

A light duration of zero selects the app's automatic mode.

On Y6RM, the app's timer labels (15, 30 and 45 minutes) disagree with its
resource names (10, 20 and 30 minutes), so the actual durations are unknown; the
bytes are sent as the app sends them. Controls that reuse a timer command under
another icon keep their own app bindings and are not treated as on/off pairs.
Additional motors keep numbered names because their physical position is
unknown.

#### Evidence

Based on Jerome's power base 1.0.9 (`com.richmat.jerome2`). Hardware is not yet
tested.

### Saatva

**App:** [Saatva](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.saatva) 1.1.0, `com.saatva`

**Status:** Not yet tested on hardware.

#### Setup

Choose **Saatva app**, then the model and installation. Adjustable Base supports
standard or split installations. Adjustable Base Plus also supports split top.
A split installation uses two receivers, which can be combined in Home
Assistant. Split top uses one receiver with separate Left and Right head controls
and a shared foot motor. Enable separate sides in the bed's options.
Split-top profiles cannot be combined as two separate receivers.

The advertised UUIDs below offer Saatva as an app choice alongside compatible
receivers. They do not identify the app or model. Setup saves the selected
profile and layout; the Bluetooth name does not select capabilities. Home
Assistant uses the receiver's saved Bluetooth address for reconnects.

#### Controls

All models have back and legs movement, Flat, Zero G, Anti-snore and two memory
slots. Plus models add TV, head and foot massage increase/decrease, massage toggle,
mode cycle, 10/20 minute timers and a light toggle button. No estimated on/off light entity is offered. Timer selection shows the last
value sent, not a measured countdown. Relative massage and light actions do not
invent measured state or absolute levels.

Split-top Right changes only head movement and head massage to bank one.
Selecting the whole bed sends both head frames; shared foot, presets, memory,
timers and light commands are sent once in bank zero. Two-receiver split beds
use the shared paired-bed controls and side targeting. Use a child for independent
head movement and the parent for synchronized foot movement, or the parent for
both heads and feet. These targets provide the app's independent, feet-sync
and all-sync behavior without changing a receiver setting.

#### Timing

Movement refresh starts immediately. Release, cancellation or the end of a
renewable hold ends the refresh; there is no STOP packet. This does not stop a
one-shot preset that is already running. Memory saves are explicit actions in
Home Assistant and send one write. The phone app uses a long press for saving;
its unused duration metadata is not a bed hold requirement. The optional
**Test head movement for 2 seconds** button requires confirmation and tests the
first head only. It is disabled by default.

#### Notifications

No application handshake, subscription, status query or position parser is
used. Motor positions, light state and massage levels are not reported.

#### Services

Use `timed_move` for back/legs movement and `stop_all` to end active refresh.
Use `goto_preset` and `save_preset` for memory slots 1 and 2. Other controls are
native buttons and the **Massage timer** select. See [Actions and
Automations](../SERVICES.md#movement-and-memory).

#### Evidence

Saatva 1.1.0 defines the model-specific controls and split-top head routing.
Physical behavior and firmware compatibility need real-user testing.

### Super Colchones

**App:** [Super Colchones](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.supercolchones) 1.0.2, `com.richmat.supercolchones`

**Status:** Not yet tested (app-derived support)

#### Setup

Choose **Super Colchones app (AFEG302, AFEG350) · Richmat** and the product printed on your
bed: **AFEG302** or **AFEG350**. Discovery matches the case-sensitive substring
`QRRM`. The `NLRN` and `NMRN` product metadata do not select a product from the
Bluetooth name. The product is always an explicit setup choice.

Six GATT routes are supported. The first supported WRITE-property characteristic
and first NOTIFY-property characteristic are retained in discovered service
order. A later supported service selects framing independently of those roles.
The actual notification characteristic need not match the nominal notify UUID.
Nordic uses framed commands; the other five routes use raw command bytes.
Writes use without-response only when the selected writable characteristic
supports it. No PIN, forced bonding or required MTU is added.

#### Controls

Head and foot movement and flat are common to both products. AFEG350 adds lumbar,
light toggle, foot massage, massage mode/all-off and a 10/20/30-minute timer select.
AFEG302 has one memory and head massage; AFEG350 has two memories. Both have
anti-snore and zero gravity. AFEG350 also has coaxing sleep mode.

Each preset's alternate byte is offered through a **Save** button. Named preset
saves ask for confirmation; numbered-memory saves use the card's **Set** mode.
The alternate bytes come from the app; save/program intent follows the app's
three-second preset gesture. Their physical effects have not been verified.
No numeric massage range, decrement or light on/off state is inferred from a
cycle/toggle command. Timer state is unknown until a successful timer write.

#### Timing

Movement starts on the first 100 ms tick. Releasing before it sends neither
movement nor STOP. A held operation refreshes until its deadline or cancellation,
then sends the app's global STOP on its captured connection with a fresh
cancellation event. Expired queued ticks are discarded at dispatch; the small HA
scheduling allowance at an exact end tick is listed above. Preset recalls and
alternate saves send once. Save buttons replace the app's three-second gesture
with the card's confirmation dialog or numbered-memory **Set** mode.

Initialization subscribes first, then sends exit-limit, clock-capability and
light-capability queries once in that order. These replies do not gate controls.
No automatic retry, auth handshake or minimum idle-write spacing is inferred.

#### Notifications

Common state and checked extension records are retained in a disabled diagnostic
sensor. Inherited parser support does not enable extra controls or calibrated
position feedback. Alarm records preserve `field_7`, `field_f`, `field_17`,
`field_1f`, `field_27` and `field_2f`; no calendar meanings are assigned.
Diagnostic detail events retain an empty details object.

Every new notification cancels the old residual-buffer deadline. Residual bytes
left after parsing expire after 500 ms. Expiry only clears, without parsing;
a late suffix cannot complete an expired prefix. Malformed unchecked accesses
are dropped safely and zero-progress extraction is bounded. Common messages
retain their source splitter's embedded-header behavior and unchecked checksum.

#### Services

Shared `hold_control`, `timed_move`, `move_to_preset` and `save_preset` actions use
the selected product's controls. Clock/alarm replies are diagnostic only: this
app has no clock-setting or alarm-programming producer, so `sync_clock` and
`set_alarm` are unavailable for this profile.

#### Evidence

Super Colchones 1.0.2 supplies both products, six GATT selections and both wire
formats. Its final automatic anti-snore BLE command is the same anti-snore recall
exposed here. Microphone/audio detection is outside this integration.

### ENSO Sleep Control

**App:** ENSO Sleep Control (Enso 2) 1.0.7 (8), `com.richmat.enso2`

**Status:** Not yet tested on hardware.

#### Setup

Choose **ENSO Sleep Control (Enso 2)** and the remote layout shown in the app.
Recognized Bluetooth prefixes suggest a layout. Cool Touch and 209A05 need
manual selection of the layout code, and parent screens such as ZRS0 offer
their control pages. The same names and services appear on other Richmat
receivers, so select the app explicitly. No app PIN or pairing handshake is
required. The controller checks both characteristic roles on the first
matching fixed service before writing. Enable **Property-based Bluetooth
receiver** only if the app uses the third-service fallback. A read-only
response characteristic allows raw keys but provides no notification data.

#### Controls

The selected layout supplies the motor covers, fixed and saved positions,
massage, light and other direct controls. Motor numbers follow the keys on
the remote. Layouts with a selector offer it on framed receivers: the nine
the app labels Left and Right as **Controlled side**, the six it labels Mode 1,
Mode 2 and Mode 3 as **Control mode**. Raw receivers always send the raw key,
and direct accessory writes use their own frames on either receiver. The
Left/Right mapping has not been verified on a bed.

E3RM has separate held recalls and confirmed Save buttons for memories 1–4.
YFRM, YGRM and BRRM can change between Press and hold and Press and release;
the controls follow that choice. U3RM starts its selected motor on motor 3.
Zero gravity 2 selects motor 3, the zero gravity, TV and anti-snore controls
select motor 4, and Lounge selects motor 5. Home Assistant retains the
selected motor through its Bluetooth handoff. GVRM provides the working first-zone
adjustment keys. Its alternate zone supplies no decoded command.

#### Timing

Held keys repeat every 150 ms, 110 ms for names starting TWRM or MLRM, and
170 ms for raw-key receivers whose name starts 6BRM. Release uses END on the
same mode and connection as the key. Save uses the confirmed alternate
action with the layout’s threshold. E3RM saves immediately after confirmation
and ends after the 50 ms release delay. A cancelled hold cannot stage further
keys on a subsequent connection.

#### Notifications

The receiver assembles checksum-valid alarm, LED and aroma notifications.
A compatible LED reply enables the color and auto-off settings. Aroma schedules
need the aroma presence reply. Alarm menus use only the current layout’s alarm
tags. A direct alarm button can expose those choices without the separate
alarm capability reply. No motor position or battery feedback is reported.

#### Services

Use [Hold control](../SERVICES.md#hold_control), [Set alarm](../SERVICES.md#set_alarm)
and [Enso 2 accessories](../SERVICES.md#enso2-accessories). Set alarm counts
wall-clock minutes to the next occurrence of the selected time and supports
only the layout’s available position and massage combinations.

#### Evidence

The Android artifact was selected on 2026-07-14. Frozen vectors cover both key
encoders, capability exchange and the direct settings writes. The Android
sender’s E3RM staging and release interleavings remain unverified. Home
Assistant owns staging and release independently.

### Dream Sense Bed

**App:** [Dream Sense Bed](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.dreamsense) 1.0.4, `com.richmat.dreamsense`

**Status:** Not yet tested on hardware.

#### Setup

Choose **Dream Sense Bed**, then **Blue**, **Green**, **Orange** or **Yellow**,
matching the app. **Saved product** choices reproduce the exact product name
already saved by the app; a remote label does not identify a product. Only the
four colors appear in the normal app chooser. Home Assistant retains the chosen
product across restarts and keeps each paired side's product data separate.

Case-sensitive names containing `QRRM`, `COOL`, `MPE_`, `209A` or `BED-` offer this
app as a candidate. Shared services and names never choose its product. The
**Controlled side** select offers Right only for products that offer sides and a
link that encodes them. The selected side survives controller rebuilds for that product. On a link that
cannot encode sides, choose **Left** to recover from a retained Right selection;
Right movement is rejected and STOP remains available. The last discovered
framing also restricts choices while the bed is disconnected.
Green, Orange and Blue separately offer split/standard control. The
**Synchronization** switch, on products with Sync on and Sync off, starts disabled.

#### Controls

Direction buttons support `hold_control`. Flat, presets, saves and massage keep
their own gestures. Confirmed saves never have a renewable hold. Fixed massage
timers use the shared duration select; intensity steps do not imply absolute
levels. L2RM has no combined Down control: the app's generated counterpart has
no known physical meaning. RGB conversion matches the app. The physical
vibration effect and measured position mappings remain unverified.

##### Startup and settings

| Operation | Frame / behavior |
|---|---|
| Initialize, once after subscription | `6E 02 01 00 71` or single byte `00` |
| CheckClock | `6E 08 01 01 78` or single byte `01` |
| CheckLight | `6E 0A 00 01 79` or single byte `01` |
| CheckMusic | `6E 15 01 01 85` or single byte `01` |
| Split control | `6E 20 09 0B 02 01 00 00 A5` |
| Standard control | `6E 20 09 0B 02 01 00 02 A7` |
| Read split mode | `6E 20 08 0B 02 00 00 A3` |
| Light duration: always on / 300 seconds | `6E 0B FF FF 77` / `6E 0B 01 2C A6` |
| RGB example: red | `6E 0C FF FF 78 6E 0D 00 00 7B` |
| Light off, side 0, no release | `6E 01 00 75 E4` |
| Vibration mode, side 0, no release | `6E 01 00 D6 45` |
| Single alarm: cancel | `6E 05 00 00 73` then `6E 06 00 00 74` |
| List existing repeat alarms | `6E 20 08 05 01 00 00 9C` |
| Update existing alarm 1 example | `6E 20 0D 05 01 01 01 01 45 07 1E 00 0E` |
| Delete existing alarm 1 example | `6E 20 08 05 02 01 01 9F` |

Clock, light and music capability probes run in that order at 300 ms intervals,
without product or reply gates. Clock-enabled products also synchronize timezone
and local calendar independently of the clock reply. Clock synchronization uses
shared sync_clock. Alarms require a current clock reply and the selected product’s
alarm choices. Lighting settings and light off require a current light reply and
the product’s lighting flag. Vibration mode requires the product’s vibration page
and a music-capability reply; no audio action is exposed. Green, Orange and Blue
offer split/standard control independently of GATT framing.
<!-- /generated -->

#### Timing

The app uses a 100 ms write queue with no command retry. A held arrow first writes
at 100 ms and refreshes until release. Ending before that first tick sends no
movement or STOP. Cleanup drains on the original connection and side only after
a control write. Single configuration and preset callbacks have no invented STOP.
Startup runs once after subscription, before the product menu. Clock sync does
not wait for the clock reply. Menu probes run regardless of product flags/replies.

#### Notifications

Current-session clock, light and music replies enable their product-gated pages.
Ordinary frames retain the app's splitting behavior, including early consumption
of ordinary fragments. Extended records wait for their length and pass sum8
validation. Pending bytes expire after 500 ms and are cleared. Alarm list/push
records and standard/split replies update connection-scoped state. Retired-session
notifications cannot change the current state.

The library's angle and status events are not used as motor positions.
No position slider or guessed range is exposed. Disconnect clears observed alarm
records and commanded settings. Stored capability knowledge may retain entity
visibility, but never admits writes on a new connection.

#### Services

A light duration control appears once lighting support has been reported. On
every product but Blue it is the **Light duration** number, 0 to 900 seconds as
on the app's slider (always on and 1 to 15 minutes); zero means always on.

On the Blue product it is the **Light timer** select, with the eleven durations
the app's slider shows. That slider sends its own position (1800 to 28800 in ten
steps of 2700) and shows these durations for it, so the select offers what the
app shows and sends what the app sends. The real duration on a Blue bed is not
verified.

| Blue's light timer | Sent |
|---|---|
| 30 min | 1800 |
| 40 min | 4500 |
| 50 min | 7200 |
| 1 hour | 9900 |
| 2 hours | 12600 |
| 3 hours | 15300 |
| 4 hours | 18000 |
| 5 hours | 20700 |
| 6 hours | 23400 |
| 7 hours | 26100 |
| 8 hours | 28800 |

Use `dreamsense_light` for RGB color and the duration in seconds: 0 to 900, sent
as given. On Blue it takes the select's durations (1800, 2400, 3000 and 3600 to
28800 in whole hours, sent as in the table) and, as before, 0 to 300 seconds
sent as given, which is no stop of the slider and leaves the select unknown.
Lighting settings and light off require a current light reply.

Clock-enabled products use shared `sync_clock` and `set_alarm`. Repeat alarm
updates require an explicit `slot` returned by the current connection's list.
Turning a repeat alarm off clears its enabled bit while preserving its record;
`dreamsense_delete_alarm` removes an existing `alarm_number`. New repeat-record
creation is unavailable. **Refresh alarms** retrieves IDs; **Alarm response**
includes the records as attributes. Both diagnostic entities start disabled.

Clock, alarm, light, split and vibration settings target the physical bed without
a side. Ordinary controls follow the selected side where supported. Audio,
phone controls, network and device administration are outside the integration.

#### Evidence

Based on Dream Sense Bed 1.0.4 (`com.richmat.dreamsense`), as delivered by
Google Play on November 18, 2026. Not yet tested on hardware.

### Likimio

**App:** Likimio 1.0.2, `com.richmat.likomio`

**Status:** Not yet tested on hardware.

#### Setup

Choose **Likimio (ABM10)** and leave the product at **ABM10** for regular controls.
Advertisements containing `QRRM`, `COOL`, `MPE_`, `209A` or `BED-` can suggest
Likimio. The match is case-sensitive. These names are shared with other apps.
The discovered GATT services determine framing. `UTRM` is a product label,
independent of the advertisement and GATT selection.

Use **No product (cancel alarm only)** for the app's fallback. This profile
offers only **Cancel alarm** after the receiver reports clock capability.

Likimio uses the same six GATT endpoint pairs as Dream Sense Bed. Nordic uses
a single command byte, and W1–W5 use checksummed frames. The endpoint needs
the write property. If the endpoint supports both write modes, the controller
writes without response. A write-only route can run ABM10's basic controls.
Advanced settings require the separate bed notification channel. Pairing
and the connection lifecycle use Home Assistant's Bluetooth stack.

#### Controls

ABM10 controls the head and feet separately or together. It offers Flat,
massage steps and fixed timers, and an underbed light toggle. You can recall
and save Zero gravity, Anti-snore, Memory 1 and Memory 2. A light capability
reply enables light duration, RGB and **Underbed light off**. Duration is 0
to 900 seconds. Zero sends the always-on sentinel.

#### Timing

Direction controls refresh while held and release with STOP after delivery.
Flat, the basic light toggle and massage send once and release with STOP.
Preset recalls and saves each send once. The alarm cancellation frames are
separate, ordered writes. Home Assistant holds commands until discovery and
setup finish, and stops sending movement when the active command is cancelled.

#### Notifications

The current connection's exact Light reply opens advanced ABM10 lighting.
The exact Clock reply opens only the no-product cancellation route. Its
**Alarm response** diagnostic shows the received acknowledgement. Displayed
light and massage settings reflect Home Assistant writes. Motor position and
device readback are unavailable.

#### Services

Use `hold_control` for a timed movement and `dreamsense_light` for RGB and
duration. **Cancel alarm** is the only action on the no-product profile.

#### Evidence

Based on Likimio 1.0.2 (10201), `com.richmat.likomio`.

### Dorsal / Roomi

**App:** [Dorsal](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.germany.dorsal) 1.0.4, `com.germany.dorsal`

**Status:** Not yet tested

#### Setup

Choose **Dorsal app / Roomi** and select **CPRN** or **CORN** to match the
app’s picker. Choose **Saved Dorsal project** for an existing four-character
project code and enter it exactly. A saved project can have an empty layout.
The Bluetooth name does not identify a project.

Choose **Roomi controls** for the Roomi page and a receiver with `QRRM` in its
Bluetooth name. The saved code is optional here and controls only the startup
queries and available alarm modes. Reconfigure checks the receiver live
before applying the route. The Roomi controls use one receiver.
Two-address combinations keep each receiver's setup separate.

Bluetooth names containing `ZRS6` or `QRRM` can suggest this app. These names
are shared by other Richmat receivers. The exact writer on one of the six
supported GATT services corroborates transport during connection. W5 is
checked on the live link.

#### Controls

| Profile | Movement and presets | Other controls |
|---|---|---|
| CPRN | Head, foot, flat, zero gravity and anti-snore | Under-bed light and synchronized movement |
| CORN | Head, foot, combined head and foot, lumbar, pillow, zero gravity, anti-snore and memory 1–2 | Under-bed light and synchronized movement |
| Saved project | Layout-specific movement, presets and memory | Some layouts add levels, timers, massage, fans, vibration, air or other accessories |
| Roomi | Head, foot, lumbar, pillow, flat, zero gravity, anti-snore, read, relax and memory 1–2 | Under-bed light, massage pattern, head and foot intensity steps and 10-, 20- and 30-minute timers |

The Save controls send the preset’s alternate command once, on confirmation.
Use [Hold control](../SERVICES.md#hold_control) for a sustained operation.
The receiver has no independently addressed left or right command on these
routes. Clock and name writes are unavailable. Raw travel and angle reports
appear in protocol diagnostics when received. Their units and the mapping
to specific actuators are unknown.

#### Bluetooth startup and release

The receiver's first exact writable characteristic and first notifying
characteristic can come from different matching services. The last matching
service selects bare or framed opcodes. Roomi widget commands always use the
framed command and framed STOP. The standard Service Changed subscription is
separate from proprietary notifications.

After each GATT setup, the controller sends Exit limit. Initial or changed
project admission adds Exit limit, Check clock and Check light at 300 ms
intervals. The movement gesture refreshes every 100 ms. Writes serialize,
and one-shot writes can follow each other as soon as the link accepts them.
Ending a hold drops pending refreshes before sending STOP. Dorsal alternates
without a release in the app send once. Roomi frame-based controls send STOP
at release.

#### Alarms and notifications

[Set alarm](../SERVICES.md#set_alarm) edits an alarm the bed reports on a
project with alarm modes. Omit the wake action to preserve the stored mode
and extra bytes. Once means an empty weekday mask.
[Manage Dorsal alarms](../SERVICES.md#dorsal_alarm) can read reported slots,
toggle or delete an existing alarm, or explicitly create or replace an
alarm. The receiver sends no end-of-list marker. A slot missing from the
list may still contain an alarm. Choose a slot you intend to overwrite
and use the table below to find the wake actions the project accepts.

Extended notifications use `6E 20 length` and a final sum8. Variable common
`6E 90` reports have no checksum test. An incomplete extended record expires
after 500 ms without another notification.

### ROOMI bed (S655 Plus)

**App:** [ROOMI bed](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.roomi) 1.0.3, `com.richmat.roomi`

**Status:** Not yet tested

#### Setup

Choose **ROOMI bed (S655 Plus)** from the bed type list or under **Dorsal app /
Roomi**. During setup, use the receiver with the case-sensitive text `QRRM`
in its Bluetooth name. The name is shared with Dorsal, so confirm the S655
Plus model before selecting this profile. A configured entry reconnects to
its saved address.

The profile uses the six [Richmat GATT routes](#dorsal--roomi) listed for Dorsal.
The service containing the first exact writable characteristic determines
framing and supplies the notify characteristic, when present. Writes use
the characteristic's advertised response mode.

#### Controls

The four motor pairs control head, foot, lumbar and pillow. Flat, preset
recall, two memory slots and under-bed light toggle are available. Each
preset and memory slot has a separate confirmed Save button. Massage
controls advance head strength, foot strength or mode, turn massage off,
and set a timer for 10, 20 or 30 minutes.

#### Timing

On each connection the profile sends ExitLimit, CheckClock and CheckLight
in that order using the [Dorsal startup frames](#dorsal--roomi). Sustained
movement starts after 100 ms and refreshes every 100 ms. Release or
cancellation ends the refreshes and sends STOP on the same link if a
movement write was attempted. One-shot controls and explicit Save actions
send one command.

#### Notifications

Bed notifications can be captured in a support bundle. The profile exposes
the light as a toggle button and offers manual anti-snore preset recall.
Position, lighting and massage feedback require hardware confirmation.

#### Evidence

Based on ROOMI bed 1.0.3 as delivered by Google Play on November 18, 2026.

### Atlas Lift

**App:** [Atlas Lift](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.atlaslift) 1.0.2, `com.richmat.atlaslift`

**Status:** Not yet tested on hardware.

#### Setup

Choose **Atlas Lift app (Cama Lift)** in the app list, or **Atlas Lift (Cama Lift)**
under **Richmat**. The case-sensitive Bluetooth local-name substring in the
table is a shared discovery hint. Choose this profile only for the Cama Lift
layout. Home Assistant selects the wire format at connection time from the
live service and its exact writable characteristic. Setup checks the same
route when the receiver is reachable. A connection with more than one
supported service is ambiguous and stops before any write.

#### Controls

Use the back and legs covers for the two actuators. Flat returns the bed to
its flat position. To save Zero Gravity, Anti-snore or Memory 1, move the bed
to the desired position and press the corresponding save button. **Head
massage up** sends one intensity step.

#### Timing

Cover presses and renewable holds wait for the first refresh tick. A finite
`timed_move` action starts with an immediate pulse within its requested
window. Home Assistant cancels pending refreshes on release and sends Stop
on the same connection after an attempted movement write. Explicit Stop
after a preset can reconnect the selected receiver in a sequential pair.
Preset recall, saving and the massage step send once. Startup sends Exit
limit mode, Check clock presence and Check light presence in order.

#### Notifications

When available, the first notify-capable characteristic on the selected
service forwards raw diagnostics. Clock and light replies do not enable any
controls. The profile exposes no measured position, light or massage state.

#### Evidence

Based on the ordinary Cama Lift layout in Atlas Lift 1.0.2. The hardware's
service assignment and physical response await validation.

### Ronco Motion

**App:** [Ronco Motion](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.ronco_motion) 1.2, `com.richmat.ronco_motion`

**Status:** Not yet tested on hardware.

#### Setup

Choose **Ronco Motion app** and explicitly select ECONOMY or PREMIUM. Names
matching the app's scan filter add a candidate beside existing detections;
shared names and GATT services never choose the layout. No PIN, account or
hardware side selector is used. Two independent addresses can use HA's paired
side routing. Each side keeps its own layout.

GATT selection follows the table's service preference. If a known role is
incomplete, a fresh property fallback uses the first non-GAP/GATT service,
the last write-capable characteristic and the last notify/indicate-only
characteristic. Combined write/notify roles are not fallback notify candidates.
The integration uses acknowledged writes, matching the app's unchanged
Android default write mode. Acceptance on firmware advertising only
write-without-response remains unverified. HA manages MTU and subscription
descriptors. It does not replay Android's stale-role or descriptor-chaining bugs.

#### Controls

Both layouts provide Head and Legs, Flat, Zero gravity and Anti-snore recall
and save, one memory recall/save, and a once alarm. PREMIUM adds Pillow and a
light toggle button. Pillow is the app label; physical actuator identity is
unverified. Light state is not inferred from toggles. No massage, measured
position, brightness, colour or second memory slot is exposed.

#### Timing

Held motor commands refresh until release or cancellation. Releasing ends
refresh without sending END. Physical stop latency remains unverified.
SHORT actions attempt their END trailer after the completed payload write,
including cancellation cleanup. An in-flight write and its trailer settle
before another action owns the link. Startup queries and alarm frames run
serially; cancellation discards unsent queries and alarm frames. A replacement
connection cannot receive the previous link's remaining frames.

#### Notifications

Only complete callback-equal alarm acknowledgements record `added` or
`deleted`. Split and coalesced alarm callbacks are ignored. Music replies
retain raw protocol diagnostic fields: four flags, signed volume and signed
intensity. Those replies do not establish music controls or measurement units.
The parser neither verifies checksums nor retains incomplete callback tails,
as in this app version. Notifications do not report position or light state.

#### Services

`adjustable_bed.set_alarm` accepts `enabled: true`, a local `time`,
and `wake_action: zero_g`, `anti_snore` or `memory_1`. The shared action requires minute precision. The once-only delay rolls
across midnight and treats equal times as tomorrow.
`enabled: false` deletes the alarm. Both operations support
`device_id` and paired `side`, validate every target before writing, and expose
only received acknowledgements, not optimistic success.

#### Evidence

Controls and timing are derived from Ronco Motion 1.2. Firmware acceptance,
physical release behavior, Pillow identity and alarm execution have not been
verified on hardware.

## Notes

### Analysis provenance

Based on RMControl, the Richmat MH apps, HJBed, Eshine, the classic apps,
Good Vibe Sleep, MLILY Control, the L&P legacy app, Casper Base 1.0.8 and Hush
Base 1.0.5, each named with its version in its section. The Richmat remotes,
Legacy BedTech and L&P MlRM routes send the pre-v5 controllers' frames.

### Base Remote

**App:** [Base Remote](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.baseremote) 1.0.1, `com.richmat.baseremote`

**Status:** Partly tested (head and feet movement on ECRM)

#### Setup

Choose **Base Remote app** in the Richmat app picker, then the four-character
layout that matches the app. The layout picker is searchable and remains available through Reconfigure.
A layout the app shows under Left and Right tabs also asks **One base, not
separate left and right sides**. Turn it on when both tabs move the same base:
each control then appears once, without a side in its name. Configure changes it.
A Bluetooth name or shared service identifies a candidate, never its feature set.
Aliases retain the app's prefix precedence; manual selection is explicit.

The first present service in W1, W2, Nordic UART, W4 order wins. An incomplete
selected service does not fall through to another data route. The advanced
third-service option selects the last writable and last readable or notifiable
characteristics of the third enumerated service. Its UUIDs require the real
receiver's GATT table. ATT writes use response when the characteristic offers it;
the Android app does not explicitly select its write type.

#### Controls

Only controls belonging to the selected layout appear. Motor 1 and motor 2 are
the **Head** and **Feet** covers where they send, on both connections, the
operands the [Richmat remotes](#richmat-remotes) move the head and the feet
with (`24`/`25` and `26`/`27`). A press moves for the bed's **Movement per
tap**. Every other motor keeps the app's number, without assigning an
unverified physical actuator, and so do motors 1 and 2 of a layout whose Nordic
connection sends another operand, or of a layout with numbered modes. Named presets,
memory, massage, locks and synchronization follow their own resource operands.
The permanently hidden lock controls are absent. Saves require confirmation and
never accept renewable holds. E3RM has separate recall and save actions rather
than an armed next-command switch.

Mode labels and commands are scoped together. Left/Right labels come from the
layout and do not establish a supported physical paired-bed topology: a single
base answers both alike, which the one-base setting is for. Nordic
ignores the mode field. U3RM's selectable motors have independent movement
buttons. GVRM's unloaded alternate getter does not become a foot command.
Hold-mode recall actions have their own Move to buttons rather than an app UI
mode selector.

The **Massage timer** select offers the slider's four stops on D1RM and D9RM (off, 10, 20 and 30 minutes: the same three commands the popup shows as 10, 20 and 30 minutes, although the slider's own stop labels read 0, 2H, 3H and 5H; the real duration is not verified on a bed),
and 10, 20 or 30 minutes on layouts with the timer popup, which has no
idempotent off. Aroma times are configuration entities, disabled by default.

#### Settings

Use the shared `adjustable_bed.set_alarm` action for the next occurrence of a
wake time, with only the selected layout's wake and massage choices. Unsupported
combinations are rejected before any target writes. The receiver stores a
countdown; the integration does not create a phone alarm or synchronize a clock
that this app cannot set.
Massage is added only when explicitly requested; omitting the zone preserves
the selected wake action without adding massage.

A valid LED reply enables the light timeout number and color settings. Layouts
with a light power control also expose the native light entity. The
`adjustable_bed.baseremote_settings` action can set RGB directly when only color
settings are available. A valid aroma reply enables three immediate time numbers.
These controls show delivered requests, not an acknowledgement of physical effect.
No phone-side draft selection becomes an entity.
Entity registry identities survive idle disconnects. Controls still require
fresh capability replies on the next connection.

The same settings action sets or removes a local Bluetooth group on receivers
with FFE0 service, FFE2 write and FFE1 notification characteristics. It writes one
ASCII command, waits before closing that physical link, and visits multiple
targets sequentially. No acknowledgement proves grouping or synchronization.
The next receiver is not configured until the preceding link has closed.
This is receiver-local setup, independent of Home Assistant's Combine feature.

#### Notifications

The shared classic parser retains fragmented data, checks additive checksums and
recognizes alarm, LED and aroma capability replies. Malformed frames are recorded in diagnostics. No live motor angle, percentage or battery telemetry exists.
Desk-only height and unit messages do not create bed state. Android's uppercase
acknowledgement checks and malformed aroma integer conversion do not establish
extra feedback or a correlation between replies and pending requests.

#### Timing and release

The worker refreshes held commands at the interval selected by the actual
Bluetooth name. Once and short-release actions emit one operand, then END.
Long actions count the node's threshold ticks before emitting, suppressing recall.
A null-short long-only release has no END on Nordic and uses the held-release
path on framed links. The original worker can retain counters and queued-write
races across touch events; Home Assistant cancels stale gestures and drains an
in-flight ATT write before cancellation-proof cleanup on the captured session.
Cleanup cannot reach a replacement link, mode or owner.

#### Limits

Physical movement, firmware effects and local group behavior remain unverified.
Phone flashlight, speech, audio, media, Wi-Fi, cloud, firmware updates, manufacturing
and stress-test tools are outside the integration. Desk layouts are outside the
bed product boundary.

#### Provenance

Based on Base Remote 1.0.1 (`com.richmat.baseremote`).

### Maxprime

**App:** [Maxprime](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.maxprime) 1.0.7, `com.richmat.maxprime`

**Status:** Not yet tested on a physical bed.

#### Setup

Choose **Maxprime app** in the Richmat app picker and confirm the four-character
layout shown by the app. A known receiver service plus a matching Bluetooth
name can suggest a layout after you select the app. The MPE and FC200 aliases
apply to Bluetooth names. The 209A05 and QRRM/COOL TOUCH receivers need the
layout code shown by the app. For a ZRS layout menu, choose its corresponding
entry in the layout picker. The picker includes the app's four-character
manual aliases. For the Russian OTRM layout, choose O0RM when the app shows
that layout.

The first present service in W1, W2, Nordic UART, W4 order selects the receiver
and requires its matching command and notification roles. Nordic UART sends
the raw resource bytes. The other three use the wrapped Richmat packet with
the selected mode byte. The advanced **Third Bluetooth service** option
allows the property fallback when none of the four fixed services is present.
It uses the last writable and last readable, notifiable or indicatable
characteristics of the third enumerated service. There is no bed PIN.

#### Controls

The selected layout and transport determine the available motor, preset,
memory, massage, light, lock, synchronization and aroma controls. Button and
hold action IDs are specific to the selected layout. A numbered
receiver mode changes the byte sent on wrapped commands. The physical meaning
of the numbered modes still needs hardware verification. U3RM's tagged presets
select the additional motor for the next movement, and the **Additional motor**
selector can change it directly. GVRM provides the head-selection commands.

BRRM, YFRM and YGRM offer **Button press mode**. **Press and hold** makes the
layout's supported recalls continuous and reveals their separate save
controls. E3RM provides explicit save and held recall buttons. Every save asks
for confirmation on the dashboard card.

The **Massage timer** select offers the slider's four stops on D1RM and D9RM (off, 10, 20 and 30 minutes: the same three commands the popup shows as 10, 20 and 30 minutes, although the slider's own stop labels read 0, 2H, 3H and 5H; the real duration is not verified on a bed).
Y6RM offers the popup's 10, 20 and 30 minutes and a separate toggle. The nine
layouts whose selector the app labels Left and Right show it as **Controlled
side**.

#### Timing

Held commands repeat every 150 ms, every 110 ms for Bluetooth names starting
TWRM or MLRM, or every 170 ms for raw 6BRM receivers. Release follows sustained
movement by 50 ms and ordinary taps by 150 ms. DXRM synchronization and
AORM/E9RM lock use their own long-press thresholds. Their completed raw
long-only gesture has no release frame, while the wrapped gesture releases
after 50 ms. The controller cancels pending writes and drains release on the
captured connection.

On a wrapped connection, startup follows successful notification setup by
300 ms. After subscription, best-effort settings probes use 500 ms spacing.
Alarm frames use 300 ms spacing and
aroma settings use 150 ms. Light duration accepts 0–300 seconds, with 0 for
keep-on.

#### Notifications

Alarm, light and aroma settings depend on replies received on the current
connection. Fragments use the classic Richmat parser's fixed widths, checksum
and wider-match precedence. An alarm set/cancel reply updates the alarm
indicator. LED replies report on or off. The bed provides no actuator position
feedback or clock synchronization.

#### Services

Use [`hold_control`](../SERVICES.md#hold_control) with the ID exposed by a held
button and [`set_alarm`](../SERVICES.md#set_alarm) for one countdown alarm.
[`richmat_classic`](../SERVICES.md#richmat_classic) refreshes capability replies
and sets the RGB color or all three aroma timings.

#### Evidence

Based on Maxprime 1.0.7 (11), `com.richmat.maxprime`, from the frozen
2026-07-14 acquisition.

### Dreamlab Control

**App:** [Dreamlab Control](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.dreamlab2) 5.1.8 (14), `com.richmat.dreamlab2`

**Status:** Not yet tested on physical hardware.

#### Setup

Choose **Dreamlab Control app**, then choose the four-character layout used by
the app. A recognized Bluetooth name suggests a layout. For a `209A05` or
`QRRM` receiver, enter the actual layout shown in the app or on its QR code.
Choose the destination if the app opens a layout picker. Select `O0RM` when
the app's Russian layout replaces `OTRM`.

If a Bluetooth proxy omits the local name, enter the bed's **Exact Bluetooth
name** in Advanced settings so Home Assistant can select its refresh interval.

The name and the shared Richmat service can suggest the family. Choose Dreamlab
Control explicitly when several apps share the same name and service. The
connection uses the first service present in the [classic transport order](#transports).
The **Bed without the app's usual connection** option
allows the app's legacy raw route when none of those services is present. It needs
both writable and readable or notifying characteristics on that service.

#### Controls

The layout supplies its own short, legacy short and long operands. Continuous
controls can be held. The card confirms saves, including the E3RM memory
programming action. It keeps those saves separate from renewable holds.

Framed Left and Right layouts can be configured as two sides of one receiver
once Home Assistant verifies the framed route. Other multi-mode layouts show
a **Remote mode** selector. Raw commands carry no mode byte. On U3RM,
**Selected motor** governs the shared up and down commands. Preset buttons
with axis tags also change that selection. GVRM's Head or foot control selects
the tagged binding. The app only supplies an operand for Head. Home Assistant
keeps these selections when it reconnects to the same layout.

On YFRM, YGRM and BRRM, the affected presets and Flat use Release gestures
by default. Recall and Flat send once, and saving uses the preset's long-press
binding. Choosing Hold enables repeated recall and Flat while held and makes
the separate save buttons available. This applies to M1 and M2 on all three
layouts, and to TV, Zero gravity and Anti-snore on YGRM and BRRM.

The **Preset button mode** select sends a Release or Hold action when you
choose an option. Home Assistant uses the default locally for gesture handling,
with no startup selector write or mode readback. APRM's selector leaves its
preset gestures as declared by the layout. AQRM's gestures are fixed, with
one-shot selector commands. C2RM and C9RM expose their available one-shot commands.

#### Timing

The selected operand and framed mode stay fixed through an action and its
END cleanup. The transport, delays and settings examples below apply to all
physical layouts. Dreamlab uses Home Assistant's connection and cancellation
lifecycle.

#### Notifications

The receiver's checksummed notifications identify alarm, light and aroma
support on the current connection. Light replies distinguish on and off.
Alarm set and cancel acknowledgements provide no schedule readback. Aroma
acknowledgements provide no timer readback. The light timeout and massage
timer start unknown. This app has no actuator position feedback.

#### Services

Use [Hold control](../SERVICES.md#hold_control) for continuous buttons and
[Set alarm](../SERVICES.md#set_alarm) for a receiver with an alarm. Alarm
choices follow the selected layout. Most layouts wait for the receiver to
report alarm availability. Layouts with a direct alarm button can also set it
through that binding. Use [Richmat settings](../SERVICES.md#richmat_classic)
to query accessory availability, set RGB or send the three aroma timers.
Use Home Assistant's device settings to set a display name.

#### Evidence

Validated with frozen app command literals and simulated Bluetooth sessions.
The tested Android artifact is the standalone APKPure selection from July 14,
2026.


### Silk & Snow

**App:** [S&S Base](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.silksnow) 1.0.3, `com.richmat.silksnow`

**Status:** Not yet tested on hardware.

#### Setup

Choose **Silk & Snow (S&S Base app)**, then CORE, ENHANCED or PREMIER.
Stored product profiles are also available as explicit choices. No advertisement
identifies a product. The app's case-sensitive scan keywords are `QRRM`, `COOL`,
`MPE_`, `209A` and `BED-`, anywhere in the name; they are candidate hints only.

The six N1 / W1–W5 routes use the [Richmat transport table](#transports).
The first writable matching characteristic supplies the writer. The first
notification characteristic can belong to any service. Separately, each service
overwrites generic encoding with its matched format, or W1 for an unmatched
service. An unmatched service never supplies a writer through that fallback.
Write-without-response is used only when that writer supports it. These choices
are settled for the current connection and cleared when it disconnects.

Only products with the side flag offer opt-in one-address left/right controls,
after a connection proves framed encoding. Home Assistant's Both target sends
the two side frames separately. The current three products have no side selector.

For ENHANCED and PREMIER, the first light turn-on chooses white when no color
has been selected or reported. Later turn-ons reuse the chosen color. Power
remains unknown until the bed reports it. The Model sensor shows the selected
product; raw reports are available in protocol diagnostics.

positions. ENHANCED adds lumbar and massage. PREMIER adds pillow and bed-light

The normal motor, preset, memory, massage, lighting and fan/heat controls use
Home Assistant's native entities and dashboard sections. Light color, power and
timer controls require the bed's light-availability response on this connection.
The product chooses white-light versus RGB-light settings. RGB modes include
cycling, flowing water, multicolor, breathe, spectrum, energy, rhythm and scroll.
White timers retain half-minute precision; RGB timers use whole minutes.

#### Timing

Writes wait one 100 ms queue tick. Movement repeats and ends with STOP on the
same attempted physical link and side. A cancelled command that never attempted
a write sends no cleanup; cleanup never moves to a replacement connection.
Presets, fan controls and immediate massage icons send once, with no release
packet. Named preset and memory programming use their own program commands.

Massage text controls (10/20/30-minute timers and all-off) can also be called
through **Hold control** using their catalog action names. Releasing or
cancelling before three seconds sends the short command. At three seconds the
app's null-long fallback emits opcode zero once and suppresses the short command.
It has no established hardware meaning and is not a save operation. Release
sends no additional packet. White-light timer changes add a 200 ms delay.

#### Notifications

Checksummed extended frames support fragmentation; ordinary common frames
retain the app's next-header boundary behavior. Common frames have no checksum
validation. Malformed extended lengths are rejected. Reports retain raw motor
indices and angles without mapping them to physical axes. The disabled-by-default
S&S Base diagnostic sensor holds bed mode, raw massage data, light reports,
alarm responses and diagnostic events. No position sliders or guessed state are
created. Reports and permissions are cleared on disconnect.

#### Services

Use **Set alarm** with `enabled: false` to cancel a legacy countdown or delete
one of the seven repeating slots on a product with repeating alarms. Both
require a fresh alarm-availability report. **Refresh alarms** requests the
repeating list; **Sync clock** writes local time on repeating-clock products.
Light settings and alarms apply to the whole receiver; target the parent bed,
not a one-address child side.
Creating alarms is unavailable: the legacy stored-action map and the exact
normal-versus-split wake-position selector still need verification. Set new
alarms in the app until those routes can be enabled without guessing.

Wi-Fi setup, network administration, cloud/accounts, updates, audio, unrelated
mattress and sleep companions are outside this integration's bed controls.

#### Evidence

Based on S&S Base 1.0.3. Hardware behavior remains unverified.

### Home Zone Adjustable

**App:** [Home Zone Adjustable](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.remedy) 1.0.3, `com.richmat.remedy`

**Status:** Not yet tested with hardware.

#### Setup

Choose **Home Zone Adjustable** explicitly in the app picker, then the four-character
layout shown by the app or its QR code. Choose a destination when the app shows a
layout picker. `209A05` and `QRRM` require the actual bed layout. Use `O0RM` for
the Russian replacement of `OTRM`. Shared services do not identify a layout.

The app's first present service wins: W1, W2, Nordic UART, then W4.
The advanced fallback option permits the third discovered service's last writable
and readable or notifying characteristics, only when none of the fixed services
is present. Supply the exact Bluetooth name if a proxy omits it.

#### Controls

The selected layout supplies numbered motors, combinations, presets, memory
recall/save, massage, locks, synchronization and lights where it has those controls.
Motor numbers do not establish physical axes. Modes remain the layout's own
selector: Left/Right or Mode 1/2/3. Nordic commands have no mode byte.

E3RM's Program selector arms one save. YFRM, YGRM and BRRM offer Hold/Release
selection for the affected presets and Flat. Head/foot and selected-motor controls
use the selected binding. A missing alternate operand does not create another motor.
Factory diagnostics, desks and phone/media controls are not offered.

#### Timing

The sender refreshes at 150 ms, or 110 ms for TWRM/MLRM Bluetooth names.
Nordic 6BRM uses 170 ms. Framed initialization follows notification setup by
300 ms. Held controls end with their selected mode's release after 50 ms;
once/short gestures use 150 ms. Long presses use their control's threshold.
Home Assistant bounds holds and drains admitted writes before cleanup, and never
continues a command or its release on a replacement connection. Standalone Stop
also releases the selected remote mode.

#### Notifications

Checksum-validated replies reveal alarm, light and aroma availability for the
current connection. Alarm acknowledgements do not report a scheduled time.
No bed positions or measured motor states are reported. Unknown fields remain
in protocol diagnostics. Reconnecting clears received capability state. The light
timeout keeps its entity identity and user customizations while disconnected;
its value is unknown and writes require a lighting reply on the current link.
The last delivered timeout is saved as a preference and is never replayed.

#### Services

Use **Set alarm** for the layout's wake presets and optional massage combination.
The bed receives the minutes remaining until the occurrence selected when the
request arrived, accounting for connection or command-queue delays. **Home Zone
Adjustable settings** queries accessory availability and controls color, light duration,
aroma times and the layout's massage slider or popup. RGB uses one concatenated
write. Light duration zero means keep-on. Settings are requests, not measured state.

#### Evidence

Based on Home Zone Adjustable 1.0.3 (4), `com.richmat.remedy`.

### Innova Control

**App:** [Innova Control](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.innova2) 1.1.0 (10), `com.richmat.innova2`

**Status:** Not yet tested on hardware.

#### Features

Controls follow the selected remote layout: movement, presets, memory recall and
save, massage, light, lock and sync buttons. Optional light color, light timeout,
aroma settings and alarms become available after the current connection reports
the corresponding capability. There is no bed position feedback. Extra motor
numbers retain their app names; their physical geometry is unverified.

#### Detection / Setup

Search for **Innova Control app** in setup, then choose the remote code used in
the app. Model pickers offer their concrete sublayouts. The similarly named
INNOVA (`com.ore.sfm`) is a separate profile. A matching transport does not
identify a remote layout. Generic third-service fallback requires explicit opt-in.

Mode 1, Mode 2 and Mode 3 remain logical modes. They do not establish physical
left/right controls. Two independent configured receivers can use HA's paired
bed routing with each side's own layout and settings.

Short, old-short and long operands are distinct. Raw connections use old-short
when present; wrapped connections use short. The memory programming selector,
Hold/Release selector and axis selector retain each layout's behavior. The GVRM
foot branch has no payload and remains unavailable.

Use `adjustable_bed.innova_control` for capability queries, RGB, light timeout,
aroma settings, timer slider positions, popup choices and Bluetooth grouping.
Use the shared Set alarm action for alarms, including supported preset/massage
combinations. FDRM and FFRM also offer their second zero-gravity alarm preset,
with no matching preset/massage combination. Timer positions and popup widget IDs are literal app choices;
physical durations are not established. Light timeout zero keeps the light on.
Aroma values are requested settings, without a working device-state parser.

Grouping sends an ASCII group name on the FFE0 service, FFE2 write and FFE1
notification channel. Choose four printable ASCII characters, or leave the
group. The selected receiver disconnects after the write; no group acknowledgement
or physical synchronization guarantee is available.

#### Position Feedback / Notifications

The parser uses the app's ordered prefix and checksum matching, including its
fragment accumulator and coalesced-frame loss. Malformed packets are bounded
and rejected safely. Alarm, lamp and aroma capability reports belong to the
current physical link. Alarm acknowledgements are events, not confirmation of
a saved schedule. No app preferences authorize writes after reconnect.

#### Command Timing

Held commands refresh until release. Long presses send once after the selected
node's threshold; short release is suppressed once the long action fires.
Framed initialization waits for successful notification setup. Settings queries
are separated by 500 ms, alarm writes by 300 ms, and aroma/RGB updates by 150 ms.
HA serializes commands and drains cancelled GATT writes before sending release
on the original connection. Cancelled actions cannot continue on a replacement
connection. No app-level retry is added.

#### Notes

The Android app conditionally queues the existing STOP when it receives a
ringing broadcast, gates touch input until idle, and does nothing on off-hook.
HA uses its own command cancellation and STOP lifecycle. Phone permissions and
broadcast delivery are not part of HA, and this does not promise immediate or
universal hardware stopping. Factory test and motor-programming screens are not
bed-control profiles.

##### Analysis provenance

Based on the accepted APK Protocol Audit of Innova Control 1.1.0 (10),
`com.richmat.innova2`, including its complete split delivery.

### Purely Sleep

**App:** [Purely Sleep](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.purely_sleep) 2.0.1, `com.richmat.purely_sleep`

**Status:** Not yet tested on hardware.

#### Setup

Choose **Purely Sleep** from the Richmat app list, then select **NXPS200
(JLRN), normal mode** or **PS200 (VJRM), normal mode**. Detection: none. A
shared Bluetooth name or service does not choose either product. These are the
only supported Purely Sleep products; the app's other models and version-one
controls are unavailable.

The runtime requires exactly one of the supported services, its exact write
characteristic with the WRITE property, and a notification channel. It uses the
first NOTIFY characteristic on that service; the declared notify UUID is not a
selection requirement. A write uses without-response only when its selected
characteristic also offers that property.

Two physical addresses can use Home Assistant's paired-bed controls, retaining
each side's selected product. Single-address split controls are unavailable.

#### Controls

NXPS200 exposes head, foot and combined head-and-foot movement; flat/reset; TV,
anti-snore, lounge, zero gravity and M1 recalls; and a separate save for each of
those five positions. PS200 exposes head and foot movement, flat/reset, and M1
recall/save. The app's PS200 torch operates the phone and is not a bed light.
The normal profiles expose no massage, bed-light control or position feedback.

Save buttons are separate from recalls and require confirmation in the native
card. A save sends once; it does not require a prolonged hold.

#### Timing

Held axes start on the first refresh tick. Writes share the FIFO interval shown
above. Releasing or cancelling a movement ends refresh and sends the explicit
STOP after an in-flight write settles. STOP uses the same ordered write path;
it does not flush or jump ahead of pending writes. Flat/reset, recalls and saves
send once without appending STOP. The integration does not retry these writes
or treat their completion as a bed acknowledgement.

#### Notifications

Complete common replies can report clock availability, light availability and
protocol version as diagnostic state. These flags do not enable additional
controls. A reported version of one blocks normal commands, including queued
writes, while keeping STOP available. A known version-one value stays blocked
across controller replacement, reconnects and Home Assistant restarts for the
same physical address and selected product, until a new version reply changes
it. Selecting another product uses that product's own retained state. Extended
and fragmented response parsing is unavailable; unknown notifications remain in diagnostics.

#### Services

Use `adjustable_bed.goto_preset` and `adjustable_bed.save_preset` with slot 1
for M1. Native buttons provide the named recalls and saves. `timed_move` and
`stop_all` use the same session, product gates and release path as the covers.
Both-side preset buttons check every physical side's version before either
side sends its command, including when a button predates the version reply.

#### Evidence

Based on Purely Sleep 2.0.1 (20103), selected normal NXPS200/JLRN and PS200/VJRM
controls. Hardware behavior has not yet been verified.


### MotionFlex

**App:** [MotionFlex](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.motionflex) 1.0.2 (10200), `com.richmat.motionflex`

**Status:** Not yet tested.

#### Setup

Choose **MotionFlex app** and select SN300, SN500 or HC800. Shared Bluetooth
names and services offer an app choice, but cannot select the model. The model
owns the motor layout, massage and angle settings. Each physical bed in a
two-address pair keeps its own model. Single-address split controls are unavailable.

The [Richmat transports](#transports) apply. In service enumeration order,
the first matching characteristic with `write` supplies the write handle and
the first `notify` characteristic supplies the subscription. Encoding follows
the last supported service, independently of those handles. A characteristic
with both write properties uses no response; write without response alone
cannot supply the write handle.

#### Controls

Head and feet are available on all three models. SN300 also moves them together;
SN500 adds lumbar and pillow, and HC800 adds lumbar. Preset recall and Save are
separate actions. SN300 includes TV and one memory; HC800 includes one memory.
All models include zero gravity and anti-snore with separate Save buttons.

Massage provides head/foot strength cycling, mode cycling, all-off and duration
choices. The basic bed-light action is a toggle. Advanced RGB, light duration
and a separate light-off button appear after the connected bed reports its light
capability. Native RGB Off sends that dedicated close even when the displayed
state is already off; turn-on continues through the color builder. The basic
toggle remains a separate button. RGB accepts integer byte channels; duration
supports always on and
the slider's minute steps. Both motor-page light icons correspond to the same
bed-light action.

#### State and feedback

Protocol diagnostics retain selected capability, alarm acknowledgment,
massage, light and numbered motor observations. Motor observations do not
become position sensors or sliders.
Malformed extra frames are rejected. Common-frame fragmentation retains the
app's limited delimiter-based behavior. Raw notifications remain available in
support diagnostics.

#### Startup and session

After subscribing, the controller sends ExitLimit, synchronizes the clock using
Richmat `record_20_len` timestamp/zone and local-calendar records, then queries
the clock and light menu. Settings builders stay framed on Nordic too.

Motor release, flat, massage and basic-light cleanup sends STOP to the exact
client that received the command. Preset recall, Save and advanced light-off
are one-shot writes. Cancellation waits for an in-flight write before cleanup.
A changed client or session cannot continue the old operation or update its
state. Replies and reported menu permissions are cleared when the link retires.
If disconnect leaves the exact owned client connected, notification restoration
binds a new session identity, keeping callbacks from the retired subscription inert.

#### Actions and automations

Use the native motor, preset, memory, massage and light entities. The shared
`set_alarm` action accepts one local alarm with a model-supported wake preset;
weekdays and additional alarm fields are unavailable. The countdown must remain
positive and fit the unsigned two-byte minute domain. Acknowledgments confirm
the completed two-frame write; partial writes leave alarm state unknown.
The shared `sync_clock` action refreshes the local clock.

### AW MOTION

**App:** [AW MOTION](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.awmotion) 1.0.1, `com.richmat.awmotion`

**Status:** Not yet tested on hardware.

#### Setup

Choose AW MOTION and the model: SilentNight SN300, SilentNight SN500 or
HighClare HC800. Shared Bluetooth names offer an app choice and do not select a
model. The first writable characteristic and first notifying characteristic are
selected independently from recognized services. The last recognized service
selects basic command framing. A characteristic must advertise write support;
write without response is used when also supported. Setup requires notifications.
No app PIN or explicit bonding exchange is needed.

#### Controls

All models have head and feet controls, flat, massage strength and mode steps,
massage off and timers. SN300 adds combined head/feet movement and TV; SN500 adds
lumbar and pillow; HC800 adds lumbar. Preset save controls require confirmation.
A light-capability reply enables direct light off, the RGB action and the duration
number. A clock-capability reply enables the single countdown alarm. The alarm
uses Home Assistant's local time; recurring alarms and clock synchronization are
unavailable. Controls and exact frames are generated below.

<!-- /generated -->

#### Timing

Held directions first send on the first refresh tick and release with STOP.
Flat, motor-page light toggles and massage controls send once followed by STOP.
Preset recall, confirmed saves and direct light settings send without an extra
STOP. Home Assistant serializes writes, never retries a failed command, and
rejects work from an obsolete connection or model. This avoids the app sender's
overlapping asynchronous timer callbacks. No audio capability query is sent.

#### Notifications

Clock and light availability and alarm acknowledgements gate optional controls.
The diagnostic Bed report sensor retains raw motor identifiers, version, mode,
massage and extended light/detection reports. Those identifiers are not mapped to
physical axes, and no position slider or angle cover is exposed. Common replies
split at the next header without a general checksum check; extended replies use
length and checksum. Malformed nonprogressing frames are discarded. Raw
notifications remain available in support captures.

#### Services

Use the generic alarm action for one local countdown or cancellation. The
`adjustable_bed.dreamsense_light` action also accepts AW MOTION devices and sets
RGB color and duration. The duration number accepts seconds; zero means always
on. These physical-bed settings reject logical-side targets. Two-address pairs
retain each side's selected model; there is no single-address side selector.

#### Evidence

Based on AW MOTION 1.0.1. Physical effects and service availability need user
validation after release.

### My Side

**App:** [My Side](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.myside) 1.0.6, `com.richmat.myside`

**Status:** Not yet tested on hardware.

#### Setup

Choose **My Side app**, then the Deep Relax Smart product shown in your app.
The four products are explicit choices. Shared receiver services and scan-name
substrings (`QRRM`, `COOL`, `MPE_`, `209A`, `BED-`, case-sensitive) cannot identify
the app or product. These words can occur anywhere in the advertisement name.

The normal products use Nordic UART or WiLinke W1 to W5. The first eligible
write and notify handles are retained independently. The last accepted service
selects one-byte or checksummed ordinary encoding. Write mode follows the
retained handle's write-without-response property. Other product selections and
the separate sleep-sensor connection are currently unavailable.

Single-address side addressing is unavailable. Two separately configured
receivers can use the integration's paired-bed controls, with each receiver's
own product settings.

#### Controls

All products have head and foot covers, Flat and two recall/save memory slots.
Coaxing adds combined head/foot movement, anti-snore, zero gravity, TV, a third
memory, save buttons for those three named presets, Coaxing mode, massage
strength buttons, mode, off, and 10/20/30 minute massage timers. No light, fan,
audio, anti-snore settings switch or motor position feedback is exposed.

#### Timing

Directions first send after 100 ms, refresh every 100 ms, and send STOP on
release or cancellation. Massage strength sends once and then STOP. Preset
recall and save are single writes. The transport spaces writes by 100 ms and
does not retry failed writes.

`hold_control` also accepts Flat and massage timer controls. A three-second
hold sends their missing long opcode zero and suppresses the short action.
Zero has no established hardware meaning. These text gestures add no STOP.
A Home Assistant STOP suppresses a pending text action. Only directional
controls accept renewable holds.

Notification subscription precedes startup. After one second, the controller
queries alarm, light and music capability. Coaxing synchronizes the local
calendar; Sleep products query the sensor advertisement name. Capability
replies cannot enable controls absent from the selected product.

#### Notifications

Protocol diagnostics include this connection's capability replies, alarm list and
linked sleep-sensor name. Valid alarm list replies append distinct
records by alarm number, replacing older fields for that number. Updates also
reconcile pending writes. Alarm records retain their unknown U byte. Editing
resets U to zero; enable/disable copies only the latest reported U and schedule,
changing the enabled bit. Mutations invalidate that record until fresh readback,
and new alarm numbers stay reserved even if a write fails or is cancelled after
it starts. State clears when the connection ends, and callbacks from replaced
sessions cannot publish state.

A query starts a fresh displayed list. It does not prove the list is complete or
that omitted alarm numbers are free, even after the first reply or a new
connection. Adding an alarm is therefore limited to replacing one explicitly
deleted in this connection. A successful delete makes its number reusable unless
a newer report for that same number arrives. Reports for other numbers do not
prevent reuse. Starting the replacement write consumes that free number, even if
the write later fails or is cancelled. Querying or reconnecting never creates
free-slot proof. An empty receiver cannot currently be populated through this
route because no complete-list or empty-slot response is established.

Only the bed-side sensor-name linkage is available. Separate sleep measurements,
sensor settings and automatic anti-snore behavior are unavailable.

#### Services

Use `adjustable_bed.myside` for repeat-alarm `query`, `add`, `edit`, `delete`,
`enable`, and Sleep name query (`name`). Coaxing alarm modes are
anti-snore, zero gravity, TV and memory 1 to 3, with up to seven numbered alarms.
Weekdays are Monday=0 through Sunday=6; an empty list means once. Query this
connection's alarms and receive list replies before adding or changing alarms.
After a mutation, receive a fresh report before changing that alarm again.
Add uses the lowest number explicitly deleted in this connection and not
subsequently reported or reused. Targets, including paired children, are validated before writing.
The shared `sync_clock` action synchronizes Coaxing calendars.

#### Evidence

Based on My Side 1.0.6 (10600). The core controls use the Richmat codec;
`tests/test_myside_vectors.py` reproduces the app's frozen static vectors.
Hardware behavior, including the physical effect of opcode zero and STOP
delivery through disconnection, still needs testing.

### Comfort Bed

**App:** [Comfort Bed](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.comfortbed) 1.0.2, `com.richmat.comfortbed`

**Status:** Not yet tested on hardware. Covers the current ComfortCareBed product only.

#### Setup

Choose **Comfort Bed app (ComfortCareBed)**, or Comfort Bed under **Richmat**.
Setup fixes the two-motor layout and massage controls. Stored settings restore
this same profile; other products saved by the phone app are not selectable.
Shared scan-name substrings are discovery candidates and require an explicit
app choice. A live connection must have exactly one supported service, its
configured WRITE characteristic, and a NOTIFY characteristic. Mixed services
are rejected before subscribing or writing.

The **Control side** selector is local: left is the default. Framed commands
carry the selected side. Nordic commands ignore that selection, so this route
does not establish independent physical sides. Native single-address pairing
is unavailable. A running movement and its release retain the side with which
they started.

#### Controls

Back, legs, and combined head/feet covers provide held movement and Stop.
The preset buttons recall TV, Anti-snore, Zero Gravity, Lounge and two memory
positions. Separate save buttons send once on a tap; they do not require a
three-second hold. Saving changes a receiver's stored preset.

Massage offers head and foot strength steps, mode change, all off, and a
10/20/30-minute timer selector. The selector shows the last duration successfully
commanded on the current connection; changing the control side clears it.
Bed light is a button without reported on/off state. Reset and Sync on have tap
actions and three-second actions. The separate three-second timer gestures use
`hold_control` with `timer_10`, `timer_20` or `timer_30`. These callbacks send
once: a missing long code sends literal zero, which is distinct from movement Stop. An HA
hold canceled before three seconds sends neither the long action nor an
unexpected short action. Use the selector for a timer duration, or tap Reset
or Sync on for their short actions.
