#### Timing

Movement refreshes every 100 ms after the first tick. The app's outgoing queue
also paces items at 100 ms. Home Assistant drains an admitted ATT write before
sending movement Stop, including on cancellation or write failure. Cleanup
never writes to a replacement connection. A failed item is not retried.
Preset, save and massage taps send once without a movement release.

Startup subscribes first, sends ExitLimit, then waits one second before the
clock and light capability queries. The excluded music query is omitted.
ExitLimit and long-code zero have no inferred physical or stopping meaning.
Physical stopping on disconnect or backgrounding is unverified.

#### Notifications

Raw notifications remain available in support captures. The ordinary dispatcher
splits at the next `6E` marker, or dispatches a current buffer of at least three
bytes. Incomplete data expires after 500 ms. Only the exact clock and light
announcements appear in connection-scoped protocol diagnostics, without an
entity. They cannot unlock alarm, RGB, light-timer, light-therapy, fan or sleep controls for this
product. No measured position, light or massage state is claimed.

#### Evidence

This profile follows the current ComfortCareBed selection in Comfort Bed 1.0.2.
Other saved products, numeric and extended replies and optional pages are not
covered. Actual service assignments, side isolation, command meanings and
receiver completion still need user hardware validation.


### MUUEGM

**App:** [MUUEGM](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.muuegm) 1.0.2, `com.richmat.muuegm`

**Status:** Not yet tested

#### Supported models

ABF03, ABF07 and NUPG400. Select the product explicitly. Shared Bluetooth names
only offer MUUEGM as a choice; they do not identify the product or replace an
existing app selection.

#### Features

All three products provide direction controls, Flat, preset recall and save,
massage intensity steps, mode steps and a 10/20/30 minute massage timer.
NUPG400 includes pillow controls and two memory presets. ABF03 and ABF07 have
one memory preset, plus Lounge; both also have Zero gravity, Anti-snore and TV.
ABF03 and NUPG400 offer Massage off. ABF07's audio button is omitted.

ABF03 has an ordinary light toggle. ABF03 and ABF07 add a color selector and
light duration after the connected bed confirms lighting support. These are
commanded settings, with no color or duration readback. Dedicated light power
off is unavailable. NUPG400 has no dedicated light or alarm controls. Position
readings and single-address side selection are unavailable on all three.

#### Detection and setup

Choose **MUUEGM (ABF03, ABF07, NUPG400)**, then your exact product. Setup owns
the motor layout, massage capability and command timing. Bluetooth proxies and
adapter selection work as usual. Close the phone app before using the bed in HA.

##### Startup and timing

| Operation | Timing | Single byte | Checksummed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Exit limit | After discovery/subscription | `00` | `6E 02 01 00 71` |
| Check clock | First menu tick, 300 ms | `01` | `6E 08 01 01 78` |
| Check light | Second menu tick, 600 ms | `01` | `6E 0A 00 01 79` |
| STOP | After delivered movement, Reset, massage or ordinary light | `6E` | `6E 01 00 6E DD` |

Direction controls first send at 100 ms and refresh every 100 ms. Reset, massage
and the ordinary ABF03 light send immediately once and release with STOP. Preset
recall sends once; saving waits 3000 ms, then sends once, without STOP. The writer
spaces packets by 100 ms. Light duration waits 200 ms. Repeat save, enable and
delete refresh the list after 200 ms. ABF03 and ABF07 send the two clock
synchronization records before menu queries.

#### Notifications and state

Clock and light controls require the exact capability acknowledgement on the
current connection. Cached capability information preserves entity identities,
but cannot grant permission on a new link. Settings become unknown after a
disconnect. Additional decoded events are diagnostic attributes only; motor
fields do not establish physical axes, units or position support.

Repeat alarm list replies append distinct six-field records. Escalation replies
replace the first record with the same ID and ignore unknown IDs. Invalid extra
checksums are dropped. Common replies do not use a generic checksum gate.
Notification fragments remain buffered on the original connection; malformed
short records are safely ignored.

#### Services

Use `set_alarm` after the bed confirms clock support. ABF03 stores a single
alarm for the next local occurrence of the selected hour and minute, calculated
when the command executes. Its success acknowledgement updates the alarm's
active state. Turning it off sends the two cancellation writes without STOP.

ABF07 accepts repeat alarms in explicit slots 1–7. Saving supplies a new time,
wake action and repeat days; Monday through Sunday occupy bits 7 through 1,
and bit 0 enables the alarm. No repeat days means once. Saving uses a zero
reserved byte. Refresh alarms to inspect existing slots before editing them.
`muuegm_enable_alarm` enables or disables a reported alarm while preserving all
other fields. `dreamsense_delete_alarm` removes a reported slot. Changes request
a fresh list; they do not fabricate a successful readback or wait for an ACK.

`sync_clock` synchronizes ABF03 and ABF07 after clock support is confirmed. The
bed's clock format discards fractional timezone hours. `dreamsense_light` sets
RGB color and duration, with duration from 0 to 900 seconds in 60-second steps;
0 means always on. RGB frames travel as one write. Clock synchronization and
single alarms each use two separate writes. Physical settings require the whole
bed target, including when combining two separate bed addresses.

#### Limitations

Other saved product IDs, advanced mattress and health controls, control-box
mode selection and single-address side controls are unavailable. Wi-Fi setup,
network administration, cloud/accounts, OTA and audio are outside this
integration's scope. Hardware behavior remains untested.

### Thrive Sleep

**App:** [Thrive Sleep](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.thrivesleep) 1.1.2, `com.richmat.thrivesleep`

**Status:** Not yet tested on hardware.

#### Setup

Choose **Thrive Sleep app**, then **Cool flow**, **Level 5** or **Eco Comfort**.
Shared Bluetooth names suggest an app candidate, never a product. The app's
scan substrings are shared across its products; HZRN and Q3RN product metadata
do not select a product automatically.

The live connection must expose exactly one of the supported services, with a
writable command characteristic and a notification characteristic. Mixed
recognized services are rejected: the app retains the first qualifying write
and notification handles independently but uses the last recognized service to
choose generic encoding. The nominal UUID table does not establish a safe
mixed-service destination. No PIN or bond handshake is required by this route.
Separate-address pairs retain each side's chosen product. Single-address
logical side control is not offered.

#### Controls

Head, foot and lumbar controls are available on all products. Cool flow adds
pillow and fan controls; Level 5 adds pillow, Motor 3, light board, massage and
coaxing sleep controls; Eco Comfort adds massage and light therapy. Motor 3
retains its app label without assigning a physical actuator.

Massage timers on Level 5 and Eco Comfort use one select with 10, 20 and 30 minute
choices. Massage all-off is a separate control, not a timer Off option.

Numbered memory recall and explicit save controls use the product's own slots.
Named preset saves require confirmation. Lighting and alarms require a live
capability reply. The light timer accepts whole seconds, with zero meaning
always on. The timer keeps its entity identity through disconnects and is
unavailable until the current connection confirms lighting. Commanded timer
values follow successful delivery, including a write that finishes after
cancellation. RGB accepts three byte channels. Eco Comfort's therapy choices send
RGB directly; selecting a color does not send a separate power-on command.
Its ON/OFF, SLEEP SOOTHING and SM actions keep their app labels.

#### Timing

Motor refresh starts on the first periodic tick. Releasing or cancelling a hold
sends STOP with a fresh cancellation token on the same captured connection.
Writes remain serialized and paced; expired movement ticks are skipped rather
than replayed after congestion. A replacement connection never receives an old
hold's cleanup. Home Assistant adds no background movement or automatic preset
sustain that the current controls do not establish.

Startup subscribes before enabling the notification stream, sends exit-limit,
then the capability queries and local calendar. Audio queries are omitted.
An unexpected disconnect returns control to Home Assistant's connection manager.

#### Notifications

Clock and light replies open their respective controls. All three products use
repeat alarms; none opens the separate sleep-sensor tab. Level 5's anti-snore
setting requires a nonempty returned sleep-device name. Refresh its setting
with the `query_snore` operation; the switch changes state only on a bed reply.

Alarm list replies refresh reported IDs; update replies replace only existing IDs.
The product sensor shows the selected product. Returned alarm records and observed
protocol, motor and massage fields are available in integration diagnostics.
Those fields do not establish position feedback or physical angle-to-axis mapping.
Refreshing alarms retains prior records until the query reaches the bed; newer
replies take priority over that refresh. Incomplete receive buffers expire;
invalid lengths and checksums are rejected at the notification boundary.

#### Services

Use `adjustable_bed.set_alarm` with an explicit app ID from 1 to 7, time,
product-supported wake action, enabled state and weekdays (Monday through
Sunday). Empty weekdays mean once. These IDs follow the app's allocation range,
not a verified receiver capacity. Saving a disabled record clears its enabled
bit; deleting a record is a separate action. Set the bed's calendar with
`adjustable_bed.sync_clock`.

`adjustable_bed.thrivesleep` offers `light_rgb` (`rgb_color`), `query_alarms`,
`delete_alarm` (`alarm_id`) and `query_snore`. All targets pass live preflight
before commands execute. Standard movement, hold, preset and memory actions
also work through the normal entities and shared actions.

#### Evidence

Based on Thrive Sleep 1.1.2's current Cool flow, Level 5 and Eco Comfort routes.
Other stored product choices, separate sleep receivers and audio are not offered.

### TOP CARE

**App:** TOP CARE 1.0.0, `com.richmat.topcare`

**Status:** Not yet tested on hardware.

#### Setup

Choose **TOP CARE app**. The app's scan keyword is a case-sensitive substring
of the advertised local name. Shared service UUIDs alone do not select this app.
Setup and reconnect require a fresh GATT table with exactly one supported service
and its exact command characteristic exposing `write`. Multiple supported services
are rejected because the app can retain a writer from one service while selecting
its encoder from another. This is a Home Assistant safety restriction.

The first notify-capable characteristic in that service receives raw diagnostic
notifications; it need not match the declared notify UUID in the table.
When the selected writer also exposes `write-without-response`, commands use that
mode. Otherwise they use acknowledged writes. Each connection sends exit-limit
initialization once. No PIN exchange is required on this motor route.

#### Controls

Head, foot, head and foot together, lumbar and pillow together, and tilt each
have up, down and side-wide STOP controls. The combined controls do not provide
independent lumbar or pillow movement. Presets, memory, massage, lights and
position feedback are not available in this profile.

#### Timing

Holds start at the first refresh tick and can renew through the card's hold lease.
Home Assistant serializes movement writes and sends a fresh STOP after an
attempted movement, including cancellation. An in-flight write settles before
cleanup; STOP stays bound to that physical connection. A replacement connection
cannot inherit an old movement or cleanup write. Releasing before the first tick
sends no movement or cleanup. Explicit STOP remains available independently.

This host safety schedule does not reproduce the app's overlapping asynchronous
queue callbacks, which can duplicate a movement and remove an unsent STOP.
The cadence in the generated table describes the app timer, not measured hardware
response or a guaranteed delivery deadline. No simultaneous-control capability is
claimed.

#### Notifications

Raw notifications are retained only for diagnostics. Sleep sensors, sensitivity,
automatic anti-snore, common and extended receive values and firmware-conditioned
page capabilities need further static analysis. No values or units are inferred
from parser names.

#### Services

The standard `timed_move`, `hold_control` and STOP actions use these native control
names. Combined controls support the same renewable hold and paired side routing
as head and foot. Commands targeting both receivers require concurrently ready
physical links; sequential two-link operation cannot admit a both-side group.
A single-address Left/Right split is unavailable.

#### Evidence

Based on TOP CARE 1.0.0's current motor screen. Its sensor and receive surfaces
remain incomplete; physical behavior has not been verified.

## Smart Base

**Status:** Not yet tested on hardware. The 200IV2 / A8RM panel is supported.

### Known Models

Select **Smart Base**, then **200IV2 / A8RM (FEE9)**. Other Smart Base panels
and transports are unavailable. A shared Bluetooth name does not choose the app.

### Apps

| Analyzed | App | Package ID |
|---|---|---|
| ✅ | Smart Base 1.3.1 (5) | `com.richmat.smartbase` |

### Features

| Feature | Supported |
|---|---|
| Motor Control | Motor 1 and Motor 2, up, down and STOP |
| Presets | Flat, zero gravity, save zero gravity (confirmation required) |
| Lights | Bed-light toggle; RGB and timeout after a current LED reply |
| Alarm | Cancel only, after a current alarm capability reply |
| Position Feedback / Massage | Unavailable for this panel |
| Paired beds | Separate addresses; no single-address side selector |

### Setup

Choose the app and product explicitly. Use **Refresh bed settings** to send the
LED and aroma capability probes. No response is needed for the basic panel.
RGB and the 0–300 second light timeout appear after a valid LED reply on the
current connection; zero keeps the light on. The timeout is a saved local
preference, not a measured bed value. Restoring it sends nothing. Reconnect and
refresh after a disconnect to admit optional settings again.

### Protocol Details

All values use the existing Richmat checksum encoder. Motor numbers retain the
panel's labels without assigning physical head or foot geometry. Mode is fixed
at zero and does not identify a physical side. Writes use the exact discovered
P1 characteristic with the shared GATT policy: no response when that property
is offered, otherwise a write response. The Android platform's on-air write
mode remains unverified.

### Commands

Held movement refreshes until release. Home Assistant serializes commands,
drains an in-flight write before STOP and sends release with a fresh cancel
event. Flat, zero gravity and the light toggle send once, followed by release.
Saving zero gravity waits three seconds and cancels safely before the threshold.
Home Assistant ends the save action with release instead of requiring another
phone touch event.

### Notifications and State

Only exact complete five-byte notifications are interpreted: `6E 0E 00 03 7F`
or `6E 0E 00 01 7D` admits LED settings and reports on/off; `6E 09 01 00 78`
admits alarm cancellation. `6E 1A 00 01 89` records an aroma capability flag in
diagnostics, without exposing unresolved accessory settings. Unknown, malformed,
fragmented or concatenated input is retained only in raw diagnostics and cannot
grant a capability. Callbacks and pending writes belong to their original link.

### Limitations

The wider Smart Base layout catalog, alternate transports, alarm scheduling,
aroma, fans, massage and sensor extensions are unavailable. RGB records are one
GATT value; changing color does not invent an on/off or movement command. The
panel's torch controls the phone camera and is not a bed light. Home Assistant
does not reproduce the phone app's inside-CANCEL, pause/resume or cancelled
long-save hazards. Hardware timing, physical behavior and RF write mode remain
unverified.

### Positions and state

Normal QRRM only logs notifications. HJ names also reach the BB parser for raw MPE diagnostics. No 6E acknowledgement or position unit is inferred.

### Timing

Motor taps write once. A hold first emits at its scheduled 30 ms tick, then refreshes every 30 ms. Release cancels refresh without sending a STOP packet. HJ preset recalls and saves write once. QRRM exposes only Sleep recall and has no long-press programming.

### Limits

Only this app's listed controls are available. Richmat's other release, side, lighting, massage and memory features are not inherited. HJ's wider variant reconciliation remains incomplete.

### Analysis provenance

AI Bed 5.7.9 (128), `com.bedding.flutter_ai_bed`; hardware UNVERIFIED.

### Sven & Son

**App:** [Sven & Son](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.svenandson.svenapp) 1.0.4, `com.svenandson.svenapp`

**Status:** Not yet tested

#### Setup

Choose **Sven & Son (Classic, Harmony, Bliss, Platinum)**, then the model printed
in your app. This is separate from the older **SVEN & SON** Richmat app.
**Not sure** offers head and foot movement, presets, memories and massage;
choose your actual model to add its other actuators and light toggle.

Bluetooth names starting with `QRRM`, `QJ-`, `LW-` or `QR-` suggest this app among
other compatible choices. Names and shared services never choose a model.
Select the base by its Bluetooth address. The app's four-character label code
is not a Bluetooth PIN and sends no authentication bytes.

The table below lists preferred writable targets in order. If none is writable,
the first writable characteristic in discovered service order is used, excluding
Generic Access, Generic Attribute and Device Information services. Writes prefer
without response. Notifications are optional, using the first notifiable
characteristic in the chosen service. Setup sends no startup commands.

A split bed uses one entry per physical base. Combine these entries using Home
Assistant's paired-bed setup to control either side or both. A bed already
synchronized by its hardware needs only the primary receiver; this app route
sends no synchronization command. The connection stays open to preserve the
local massage timer and its accounting. Paired massage requires **Concurrent**
connections. Sequential connections still support movement and presets. If
Automatic falls back to Sequential because a Bluetooth adapter has too few
connection slots, massage controls require Concurrent connections again.

| Massage | Head and foot steps, levels 0–3, next pattern and compound off |
| Bed light | Model-dependent toggle |
| Massage timer | Home Assistant timer, not a firmware timer |

<!-- /generated -->

Massage levels are estimates based on commands sent by Home Assistant. On first
connection or after a lost connection, turn both massage motors off with the
remote, then press **Confirm massage is off**. Use **Confirm massage has rested**
only if both motors have been off for at least ten minutes. Otherwise wait for
the rest interval before starting massage. Remote or app changes require this
reconciliation again. Confirmations send no blind toggle packet.

The level numbers provide off, low, medium and high by sending the required
steps. Next pattern requires an active zone and resets each active zone's
estimated level to low. Massage off steps the head zone to zero before the foot
zone. If a step or release fails, the estimate becomes unknown. Select a duration only while massage is running. Its deadline stays fixed
through level and pattern changes; choosing a new duration sets a new deadline.
Without a selected duration, the accumulated-use limit still applies. The timer uses
the same off sequence; a lost Bluetooth link cannot guarantee physical stopping.
Use the remote to stop massage if the connection is unavailable.

#### Timing

See the generated timing table above. Motor taps are single presses; holds
refresh until released. Every movement exit attempts End on its original
connection. A replacement connection never receives a stale gesture's release.
Saving memory is a single confirmed action, equivalent to the app's accessible
Save action, rather than repeated programming during a hold.

#### Notifications

Notifications remain raw diagnostics. This route reports no measured position,
massage acknowledgement, light state or model readback. Massage numbers and
local timer values reflect Home Assistant commands, not received bed state.
**Last commanded preset** records a named preset; motor movement or memory recall
clears it. Its saved label is command history, not a measured bed position.

#### Services

Use the standard memory, preset, timed movement and paired-side actions. Home
Assistant automations can recall zero gravity at bedtime, request timed head
movement, or recall anti-snore. Schedules live in Home Assistant; this route has
no firmware clock or alarm. Do not leave massage running unattended after a
Bluetooth failure.

#### Evidence

Based on Sven & Son 1.0.4. Independent literal vectors are exercised by
`tests/test_sven.py` through the shared Richmat encoder.


### TSS Remote

**App:** [TSS Remote](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.richmat.tss_remote) 1.0.4 (5), `com.richmat.tss_remote`

**Status:** Not yet tested

#### Setup

Choose **TSS Remote app**, then the four-character layout used in your app.
The receiver's Bluetooth service selects the command format independently of
that layout. Shared Richmat names and services only suggest an app candidate;
they never select TSS Remote automatically. Names containing `209A05` and the
`QRRM` chooser require an explicit layout. Chooser pages are presented as their
individual layout choices. Reconfigure changes the app or layout.

The named services use the shared Classic order W1, W2, N1, W4. An incomplete
first matching service fails setup instead of borrowing another service's
characteristics. The advanced third-service fallback is opt-in and requires a
writable characteristic and a readable or notifying characteristic on that
actual service. No PIN, account or Wi-Fi setup is required.

#### Controls

| Feature | Supported |
|---------|-----------|
| Movement | Only controls whose physical meaning is explicitly labelled in the selected layout |
| Position feedback | No |
| Presets and memory | The selected layout's recall and confirmed save controls |
| Massage | Layout-specific intensity, modes and timers |
| Lighting | Layout toggle; RGB and timeout after a current lighting reply |
| Alarm | The selected layout's wake choices and supported massage combinations |
| Synchronization and lock | Where the layout provides these bed controls |
| Physical side routing | No; numbered app modes do not establish Left and Right |

Motor numbers and generic arrow/segment icons do not establish which physical
part moves. Such commands stay in diagnostics, without a guessed cover, angle
sensor, position slider or physical-axis name. The command table identifies
these as diagnostic-only. Bluetooth, audio, fragrance and factory controls do
not appear as bed controls.

YFRM, YGRM and BRRM retain their Release/Hold selection and dedicated save
buttons. Saves require confirmation and never offer renewable card holds.
APRM and AQRM provide Synchronized bed operation. A9RM provides separate Left
head and Right head movement buttons, and FLRM provides Bed height movement.
These are controls on the selected receiver; they do not select a paired side.
Fixed massage durations use the shared Massage timer select. ZWRM offers
120, 180 and 300 minutes (2, 3 and 5 hours); OTRM and APRM offer 15 and 30
minutes. Other layouts retain their own durations. No Off option is added
unless that layout has a separate supported timer-off command.

When upgrading from the separate duration buttons, one existing button's name
and user settings carry over to the select. The remaining duration buttons are
removed; Repairs identifies automations that still use them. Replace
`button.press` with `select.select_option` on Massage timer, using an option
such as `15 min` or `120 min`. Independent massage-mode and on/off actions remain.
FGRM, FMRM and FNRM expose their long-press bed lock; the
short audio action on the same widget is unavailable.

On/off pairs use one switch, including DXRM synchronization and APRM massage.
Their long-press choices keep their delay and release behavior. APRM's massage
mode button remains available independently of its long-press off choice.
Lighting uses the shared light entity when the receiver reports its current
power state. Where a light button also has a long-press off choice, turning the
light off keeps that delay; the separate long-press button remains available.
Both choices refresh power after writing; until that reply, power is unknown.
RGB and timeout require a fresh lighting response after reconnecting. RGB waits
briefly for the startup lighting reply. An RGB action targeting several receivers
checks every receiver's live lighting support before sending its first color
write. A saved capability only keeps the entity findable; it never
authorizes a write to an unverified replacement receiver.

#### Timing

The generated setup and command tables give the app's own timings. Long
thresholds use integer division by the actual repeat interval. Source worker
phase and retained counters do not prove an exact physical hold duration.
Home Assistant owns each gesture independently: cancellation stops refresh,
cancels a pending save, and drains its defined END cleanup on the captured
session. A replaced connection never receives an old gesture's command or END.

Y6RM offers 15, 30 and 45 minute massage timers. D1RM and D9RM offer the distinct
2, 3 and 5 hour slider stops. The shared timer select shows these durations in
minutes. Identical bytes across those layouts do not imply identical durations.

#### Notifications

Presence replies gate alarm and lighting settings for the current connection.
Alarm acknowledgements are diagnostic events, not a readback of the alarm time
or proof that the hardware delivered it. RGB and timeout values are commanded
values. No bed motor position, current, firmware or angle feedback is reported.

The parser preserves source length-first and prefix-search behavior, including
loss of a second coalesced record. It contains malformed input in the HA callback
and bounds the receive buffer. Old-session callbacks cannot change current
capabilities or state.

#### Services

Use **Set alarm** for supported wake presets and massage combinations. An
unsupported combination fails before any writes. A presence reply without known
wake choices permits cancellation only. The same-minute time means
the following day. The alarm uses two direct frames, independently of the
ordinary command format or selected app mode. Refreshing features uses the
optional diagnostic **Refresh bed features** button or the existing
**Classic Richmat app settings** action with operation `query`. Operation `rgb`
sets a lighting color after a current capability reply. Other app-family
settings are rejected for TSS Remote.
